- **A quick Feature's Task takes the Feature's title and description; `skill` and `workspaces` on `fileFeature` are a quick Feature's only (`invalid` otherwise), and a quick Feature cannot name `from_retrospective`; it files no Retrospective when shipped or dropped, by hand or by ship-when-done.** Why: CONTEXT.md's Quick Feature has no Retrospective, and a Retrospective files Features to be broken down.
- **Agent settings are a program (`command`) and its arguments (`args`), each a template, not one shell string. Defaults: `claude` with the Claude Code arguments of agents-plan D1, model `claude-sonnet-5-5`, no env, unattended, not paused. `setAgentSettings` merges over them; `env` replaces the whole set and `progress_file: ""` clears it.** Why: the Runner starts a process without a shell to parse quotes, and merging lets `darkory agent set builder --paused` stand alone.
- **`member.agent_changed` records the first settings whole and later ones as the fields that changed, `env` by its variables' names only; an unchanged request writes nothing.** Why: Activity is every Member's to read, and values in env may be long.
- ~~**Agent settings, `env` included, are readable by every Member; env names starting `DARKORY_` are refused.** Why: Members are one Organisation, secrets belong in the server's environment (which sessions inherit), and the Runner sets `DARKORY_URL`, `DARKORY_TOKEN` and `DARKORY_SESSION` itself. The spec says so on `AgentSettings`.~~ Sessions no longer inherit the server's environment; see "A session's environment" under the smoke run's fixes below.
- **`init` seeds its roster in its one write, recorded with the first Member as actor; each agent's token is named `runner` with a 5-minute default heartbeat timeout, written to `<data>/agents/<name>.token` (0600, the directory 0700) and never printed.** Why: agents-plan's runner step 1 takes 5 minutes, and a secret shown once on screen is one more copy than the Runner needs.
- **`init` finds the repository from its working directory; the Workspace is named after the repository's directory (characters a name cannot hold become dashes), and its default branch is the one `origin/HEAD` names, else the branch checked out, else `main`. Outside a repository the roster is still seeded, without a Workspace; `--no-agents` seeds no roster at all.** Why: `git symbolic-ref HEAD` alone would make a feature branch checked out at `init` the branch everything lands on.
- ~~**`/v1/runner/sessions` answers `no_runner` like the other Runner operations when none is attached, not an empty list; an admin check comes before it on nudge and stop; the CLI exits 1 on it, not 3.** Why: a client can then tell "no Runner" from "nothing running", and no Runner is not a rule of the record.~~ Replaced below (the lead's call, 2026-10-07).
- **Nudge and stop accept an Idempotency-Key and keep nothing under it.** Why: they act on a session, not on the record, as Heartbeat does; repeating one does what it did.
- **The terminal names the Member joining through the context (`runnerapi.ViewerOf`), since `Attach` takes only `readonly`; the server checks a browser's Origin (its own address or the public URL) before upgrading and leaves coder/websocket's own check on, the public URL's host as its pattern; a client sending no Origin, such as a CLI with a token, is not a browser.** Why: the lead's interface signature, the Note on join in D6, and cross-site WebSocket hijacking, which a GET with the cookie would otherwise allow.
- **The Runner's sessions are not filtered by Organisation.** Why: a Local Install holds one, and a Runner is Local's (ADR 0013).
- **`Task.workspace_ids` is absent when a Task names none, as `open_blockers` is; `TaskDetail.workspaces` is always there.** Why: the API's "fields with no value are omitted", while a detail lists its parts.
- **The CLI's Runner command is `darkory sessions` (with `nudge` and `stop`), not `session`, which lists a Member's Darkory Sessions; `darkory workspace set` changes a Workspace and `darkory file --no-workspace` names none.** Why: every `/v1` operation has a command, and the two kinds of session are different things.
- **The e2e harness runs `init --no-agents`, except TestBots, which runs on a seeded Install and lets `bot.Setup` keep init's planner, reviewer and retro.** Why: the other tests predate the roster and TestMVPFlow makes agents named retro and reviewer itself.
- **A Task filed naming no Workspace names its Team's default, or none when the Team has none (`workspace_ids` absent), and the Runner then starts its session in `<data>/sessions/<task-key>/` with no checkout, saying so in the prompt; `workspaces: []` names none on purpose; a named Workspace that does not exist is `not_found`; only a quick Feature filed where no Workspace would be named is `invalid`, saying how to set the Team's default.** Why: the lead approved the permissive reading on 2026-10-07, replacing the line struck above; refusing every such Task would refuse all filing on Installs and Teams with no Workspace, while a quick Feature's one Task exists for the Runner.
- **A Note on a Task nobody holds, open or ended, is open to its Feature's owner and any Member of its Feature's Team, and records no Skill; a held Task still takes Notes from its holder alone, under their Claim's Skill, in one batch. A Note read unheld is written in an ordinary write that reads the Task again under the counter, and falls back to the holder-only rule if it was claimed in between.** Why: the Runner notes merges and conflicts on review Tasks the reviewer has just completed (the lead's call, 2026-10-07), mirroring who may block a Task nobody holds and who may attach Evidence to it; the held path keeps its one round trip.
- **`GET /v1/runner/sessions` always answers 200, `{items, runner}`: `runner: false` with no sessions when no Runner is attached; nudge, stop and the terminal still answer `409 no_runner`, after the admin check on nudge and stop, and the CLI exits 1 on it, not 3.** Why: the web app polls the list, and Chrome logs every non-2xx fetch as a console error, failing every e2e page that asserts a clean console (the lead's call, 2026-10-07, replacing the line struck above); `runner` still tells "no Runner" from "nothing running", and no Runner is not a rule of the record.
- **Joining a session's terminal is treated as a write though it arrives as a GET: an upgrade signed in by the cookie must pass the same own-pages check as a cookie write (Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin when sent, the Install's Origin or Referer), any Origin sent must be the Install's, and a bearer upgrade needs none. The mode comes from the caller: read-write only for an admin who did not ask for `readonly`, read-only for every other Member whatever they ask.** Why: a GET skips the write check in the auth middleware, and a cross-site page could otherwise open a WebSocket carrying the admin's cookie (a review flagged it, 2026-10-07); this tightens the terminal line above, which checked an Origin only when one was sent.
- **`DELETE /v1/members/{member}/agent` (admin) clears an agent's settings: the Runner starts no new session for it, one running carries on until its Claim ends, and the agent works through its own tokens only; it records `member.agent_changed` with `{cleared: true}`, a human is `invalid`, and clearing none writes nothing; settings set again start from the defaults.** Why: `paused` keeps an agent the Runner's, while an agent run from elsewhere should not look like one (the web builder's finding, 2026-10-07); `darkory agent clear <member>` is its command.

### Runner (R1)

- **A merge of a reviewed Task's branch, or its conflict, is noted on that Task ("Merged WEB-12/cart-page into feature/WEB-1 at <sha> (web).") by the reviewer whose Complete merged it, when it is one of the runner's agents (else by the runner's first agent), and the Task resolving a conflict is filed by the same Member; a Note on a Task nobody holds is open to a Member of the Feature's Team (R0). A Ship's merge is Evidence `merge-<FEATURE-KEY>.txt` on the Feature, which has no Notes.** Why: the record's log is the Note, written as the Member whose token the runner acts with (the lead's call, 2026-10-07); the plan's `task.merged` kinds are not built.
- **The MCP configuration the runner writes runs `darkory mcp --no-heartbeat` (`DARKORY_MCP_NO_HEARTBEAT=1`).** Why: `darkory mcp` otherwise heartbeats its Session's Claims for as long as it runs, which would keep a hung session's Claim alive and empty D8's progress gate.
- **`darkory join <task> [--readonly] [--data dir]` joins a session's tmux pane; `darkory attach` stays the Evidence command. The loop alone is `darkory runner`, and `serve --runner=auto|on|off` (`DARKORY_RUNNER`) runs it in the server.** Why: the lead's calls; `attach` was the Evidence command, and `agents` sat one letter from `darkory agent set|list`.
- **The runner's tmux sessions run on a tmux server of its own, `tmux -L darkory-<first 8 hex of sha256(the data directory's real path)>`; `darkory join --data` finds it.** Why: the sessions stay out of a person's own tmux server and its `kill-server`, and two Installs on one machine never share one.
- **A session's environment (the token among it) reaches tmux through a 0600 `env.sh` the session's `run.sh` sources; the MCP configuration is 0600 too; neither goes on a command line.** Why: every process can read another's arguments (security review L9's reasoning for `--token`).
- **The runner records each branch it makes in `<data>/workspaces/branches.json`; a `<KEY>/…` branch the ledger lacks is never worked on, and the session is released with a Note saying so.** Why: "never touch a branch it did not create" needs a record of which it created; the repository cannot say.
- **The Feature's branch is made from the default branch whenever a Task of a Feature that is not quick needs it and it is missing, not only by the Break down's session.** Why: a Feature broken down by a person, or a Workspace added later, would otherwise leave its Tasks without a base.
- **A merge into a branch checked out nowhere is `git merge-tree --write-tree`, `commit-tree` with both parents and `update-ref` guarded by the old tip; into a branch checked out in a clean worktree (the default branch in the person's own repository, usually) it is `git merge --no-ff` there, aborted on a conflict; uncommitted changes there refuse the merge.** Why: no checkout of the person's is touched unless it is the target and clean, a conflict leaves both branches as they were, and merge-tree needs no working tree; git 2.38 or newer.
- **The runner's merge commits are by the repository's `user.name`/`user.email` when it has them, else by "Darkory runner <runner@darkory.invalid>".** Why: a machine with no git identity would refuse to commit.
- ~~**Only a Complete under `review`, or a company Skill built on it, merges a Task's branch; a Break down, or a Task completed without review, leaves its branch unmerged.** Why: ADR 0014 makes review the merge gate; the Break down's branch only holds what its planner read.~~ Replaced below: a work Task ending Done merges whoever completed it.
- ~~**A merge that conflicts, or that a dirty checkout refuses, files a work Task on the Feature, "Resolve the merge of <branch> into <target>", needing the Skill of the reviewed Task's last Claim under another Skill than review (`engineer` when none), with git's report in its description; the build Task itself is not reopened. When the Feature has ended (a quick or ship-when-done Feature ships in the review's own write) nothing can be filed, and the runner logs it for a person.** Why: the lead's call for R1, and an ended Feature takes only questions.~~ Replaced in M3 (below): the resolving Task is filed at the Step its builder worked at.
- **A Task's worktrees go when it ends, Done or Dropped, merged or not; its branches stay, and a worktree with uncommitted changes stays.** Why: a Done Task's work is in its branch (merged or not), and nothing the agent left uncommitted is thrown away.
- **A second session of a Task on one runner (the reviewer's, right after the builder's Handover) waits for the first to end, heartbeating meanwhile** (and starts the moment it has ended, below). Why: the two share the Task's worktree, log and tmux name.
- **A question the agent filed against its Task is a decision: the runner releases the Task ("Waiting for the answer to WEB-17") and it comes back through `next` once answered.** Why: a blocked Task held by a stopped session would lapse anyway, and the exit rules tell the agent to stop after asking.
- **Every release without a decision starts its Note "Session ended without a decision"; the runner counts those Notes on the Task, and the third (sixth, …) files the question to the Feature owner while it still holds the Task, then releases.** Why: the record keeps the count across runner restarts and machines, and a question filed after the release could lose the race to another claimer.
- **A session that cannot start (a missing command, a Workspace that cannot be prepared) is released the same way, and that agent pauses for the nudge interval before its next `next`.** Why: the same failure would meet the next Task at once, and three of them reach the owner.
- **The first nudge goes at the first check that sees the turn ended, the second a nudge interval later, the release one interval after that; the nudge is typed into tmux with `send-keys -l` and Enter, or written to a child's standard input.** Why: the plan's "twice, 2 min apart, then release"; a turn that ended on a question to the screen gets no answer by waiting.
- **The turn has ended when the last user or assistant message of the transcript's main conversation is an assistant message asking for no tool; Claude Code's other records after it (titles, costs, attachments, subagents) are passed over. A generic progress file's last line `TURN_ENDED` says the same, and a progress file older than the session is ignored.** Why: Claude Code 2.1 appends bookkeeping after its last message, so the literal last line rarely is one.
- **The transcript is found at `~/.claude/projects/<the working directory's real path with every character but letters and digits made '-'>/<session id>.jsonl` (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set), and by its session id in any project when not there.** Why: checked against this machine's projects (`/Users/x/.claude` → `-Users-x--claude`, `/tmp` → `/private/tmp`).
- **A command with no progress file to read (not Claude Code, and none named) counts as making progress while it runs.** Why: the runner has nothing else to gate on, and the Claim still lapses when the process hangs the machine or is killed.
- **Claude Code gets its first message, "Work on Task WEB-12: Cart page. Your instructions are in the system prompt.", as its last argument when no argument names `{task}`, after the placeholders are filled so a title is never read as one; an agent that is not unattended loses `--dangerously-skip-permissions` from any arguments.** Why: R0 stores the default arguments without a message, and interactive Claude Code waits at its prompt for one (the lead's wording).
- **The runner closes each session's Darkory Session when the session ends, and on shutdown it stops every session (`/exit`, 2 s, kill) and releases its Task with a Note; `serve` stops the Runner, up to 30 s, before the HTTP server.** Why: a Claim the runner failed to release still ends, and the last releases and Evidence reach a server that is still up.
- **`serve --runner=auto` (the default) runs the Runner when `<data>/agents` holds `<member>.token` files; the Runner reaches the server on its listen address, not its public URL.** Why: an Install with no agents should start as before, and the Runner is a client of the server beside it.
- **In a `pull_request` Workspace the runner merges nothing itself: it pushes the Feature's branch when it makes it, the exit rules tell the agent to push its branch and open a pull request into it carrying the key, a merged one completes the review (through the session that holds it, or by claiming it as the first of its agents that may), and Ship opens the Feature branch's pull request with `gh pr create`.** Why: GitHub holds the merges in that mode, and a local merge would leave the feature branch out of step with it.
- **A session's `pane.log` starts empty at each session of the Task, and its last 8 MiB are attached.** Why: the earlier session's log is Evidence already, and the Evidence limit is the Install's.
- **The darkory binary the runner is goes first on a session's `PATH`, and the MCP configuration names it.** Why: the agent's CLI and MCP server are then the same release as the runner.
- **The runner's clocks come from `DARKORY_RUNNER_TIMINGS` (name=duration pairs) for tests; `DARKORY_RUNNER_TMUX` chooses tmux for `serve`.** Why: the plan's minutes would make every scenario test take hours, and e2e must force child processes on a machine with tmux.
- **A Task that names no Workspace has its session started in `<data>/workspaces/<KEY>/`, an empty directory, not in `<data>/sessions/<KEY>/` as R0's line above says.** Why: the sessions directory holds `mcp.json`, which carries the agent's token, and the agent should not find it in its working directory.
- **The merger logs no error for a request its stopping cut short.** Why: `darkory runner` stopping mid-merge is not a failure, and the e2e log check would flag it.
- **The session's log goes on the Feature, under the same name ~~`session-<KEY>.log`~~ (now `session-<KEY>-<agent>-<HHMMSS>.log`, below), when attaching it to the Task is refused because the next holder has the Task already.** Why: the reviewer's runner claims within a second of the builder's Handover, and Evidence on a held Task is its holder's (the lead approved, 2026-10-07).
- **The terminal's mode is the server's: `Attach` takes `readonly` from the handler, which gives read-write only to an admin who did not ask to watch; a watcher attaches with `tmux attach -r -f ignore-size`, so its panel's size never resizes the agent's window, and what it sends is dropped before the pty. Only a read-write join writes "<name> joined the session."** Why: the terminal is a shell (Claude Code's `!`), and the web connects read-only on every look at a Task's page (the lead and the web terminal's builder, 2026-10-07).
- **A runner session's security posture on Local (ADR 0013, D7):** the session runs as the user who runs the Install, with Claude Code's permission checks skipped; the fence is the worktree, the exit rules and the branch ledger (the runner never force-pushes and never touches a branch it did not create). The agent's token reaches the session through a 0600 `env.sh` sourced inside tmux on a private per-Install socket, never on a command line; the browser terminal is read-write for admins only, read-only for everyone else, and a cookie upgrade must pass the same own-pages Origin check as a cookie write. Why: the human chose unattended sessions over an allowlist for now; everything an attacker could reach through the terminal they could already reach as that user, and the Origin check keeps a cross-site page from joining.

### Runner: the smoke run's fixes (2026-10-07)

The first real Claude Code session under the Runner (agents-plan.md, "Smoke run") found D1–D7; these are the calls made fixing them.

A child process gets exactly that; in tmux the pane runs `run.sh` under `env -i` with only the pane's `TERM`, and `env.sh` sets the rest; the tmux server itself is started with the same few variables. Agent settings stay readable by every Member, and env names starting `DARKORY_` stay refused; secrets go in the server's environment, named in `DARKORY_RUNNER_ENV` (the spec says so on `AgentSettings`).** Why: a serve started inside Claude Code or a person's tmux handed every session `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_*`, `TMUX` and `TMUX_PANE`, so Claude Code took itself for a nested one (smoke D2); the lead's list, plus what Claude Code needs to reach its API behind a proxy or with an API key, and a way to pass the secrets the old line sent through inheritance.

- **A session's log is attached as `session-<KEY>-<agent>-<HHMMSS>.log`, the time the session began (its Claim), in UTC.** Why: the builder's log on the Feature and the reviewer's on the Task were both `session-MAIN-2.log` on one Feature page, told apart only by who attached them (smoke D5); the agent names the session and the time orders a Task's repeated sessions of one agent, in the record's zone.
- **A session waiting for an earlier session of its Task starts the moment that one has ended: it waits on the earlier session's end, not on the progress clock, and heartbeats each Tick only while it waits; a session leaves the Runner's list before it says it has ended.** Why: the reviewer's session started 31 s after its Claim although the builder's had ended 2 s after the Handover, because the wait slept a whole Tick between looks (smoke D6); `next` had already returned at once.
- **A runner session's state is `running`, `waiting`, `stalled` or `ending` (`RunnerSession.state`), and `waiting` replaces `nudged`. The Runner works it out at each progress check: `stalled` while its progress has been stale for the stale window (the Runner sends no Heartbeats and the Claim lapses unless it moves), else `waiting` while the agent's turn has ended with the Task held and no decision (a nudge pending or sent), else `running`; `ending` once the Claim has ended, never left. An admin's nudge changes nothing until the next check. The web shows it as a pill (Running done-green, Waiting claimed-amber, Stalled blocked, Ending dropped-grey) in the Session panel's facts, the agent's peek and the Agents table, beside the Heartbeat meter, which empties by itself once Heartbeats stop.** Why: a session stalled on a dialog said "Running" with a full Heartbeat meter while only serve.log said its progress was stale (smoke D7); `nudged` said only that a nudge was sent and was never reset when the agent worked again, and the lead's four pills have no Nudged. A breaking change to an enum of a read model no released client reads.

- **A Claude Code session runs with the person's own Claude Code configuration: `~/.claude` and `~/.claude.json` under the `HOME` it passes (or the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` of the server's environment, which pass when set), with their sign-in, trust decisions, hooks, plugins, status line, `CLAUDE.md` and permission rules. The Runner sets no Claude Code variable of its own, pre-seeds neither trust nor the Bypass Permissions acknowledgement, and writes nothing in the person's files; `<data>/claude` is gone.** Why: the human's rule (2026-10-07), in their words: "NOt separate Claude Code config folder!!! This requires users to make this folder trusted before using the feature. Note that for local, it will also link to an existing repositories folders/directories that have checked out the code." It replaces the isolated directory struck above: a separate folder would need trusting before the feature works, while a Local Workspace is a repository the person has checked out and used with Claude Code, so it is trusted already, and Claude Code keys the trust on the repository, which the Task's worktree inherits (checked with Claude Code 2.1.289: a repository trusted by opening `claude` in it once, its worktree under `<data>/workspaces/` met no dialog, and `~/.claude.json` gained no entry for the worktree). The person's hooks and plugins then run in agent sessions, by their choice: a status line can print their account and usage into the session log the Organisation reads, and a hook can start sessions of its own; testing.md says so.
- **The on-screen answer to a first-run dialog stays, for a repository never opened in Claude Code: only in a Claude Code session in tmux, only before the agent's first model turn (its transcript absent or holding no assistant message of the main conversation; an unreadable one counts as answered), only when the visible pane is exactly the folder-trust dialog (naming the session's folder) or the Bypass Permissions mode warning of 2.1.289, with nothing under its "Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel", and one dialog per session. The keys are Down and Enter through `Answerer.AcceptFirstRunPrompt`, which presses nothing else, and a Note says "The runner accepted Claude Code's first-run prompt: <which>." A matching screen after the first turn gets no key: the session is `waiting` and one Note says "Claude Code shows a first-run dialog after the agent's first turn; a person can answer it with darkory join <KEY>."; a second dialog in the session is left to a person the same way ("Claude Code shows <which>, and the runner accepts one first-run dialog a session; …").** Why: the lead's guard against the agent's own output drawing a dialog (2026-10-07), the only dialog handling there is: before the first turn the model has written nothing to the screen. A repository never opened in Claude Code, for a person who never accepted Bypass Permissions mode, meets both dialogs; the Runner accepts the trust dialog and a person answers the second by joining. What Claude Code saves when the Runner accepts goes into the person's own files, as if they had answered.
- **`waiting` also covers a session showing a dialog the Runner leaves to a person** (the spec says so on `RunnerSessionState`). Why: the person is what the session waits on, and the Session panel's Join is where they answer it.
- **One Idempotency-Key gives one answer, a rule's refusal included. A write refused with a 409 code (`conflict`, `already_claimed`, `not_takeable`, `not_holder`, `ended`, `cycle`, `tasks_open`, `proposal_stale`, `status_in_use`, `use_complete`, `use_drop`: every code `statusOf` sends as 409) keeps the refusal under its key as a response is kept, and every later or concurrent request under the key gets it back. `invalid`, `not_found`, `forbidden`, `unauthenticated`, `session_required`, `too_large`, `idempotency_key_reused` and `not_implemented` keep nothing, nor does a `next` that answers 204.** Why: the e2e soak sent a claim twice at once under one key while the holder released; one was refused `already_claimed` and kept nothing, so the other then claimed the Task and one request got two answers (`TestRaceIdempotentClaimsAgainstARelease`). A 409 is the rules' answer about the record as the write found it, which the record moving on can contradict; the other codes judge the request or the caller before any rule runs, and come out the same when it is sent again. A refusal saying "read it and try again" is kept too: trying again is a new request, under a new key.
- **A kept refusal is written after the rollback by a write of its own, through `store.WriteBatchNoSeq` and outside the counter. The key's primary key serialises it with a concurrent request under the same key, whose write keeps its answer there too; whichever keeps its answer first is the answer, and the other replays it.** Why: the reason is read only after the rollback (invariant 4), so the winning path keeps its one round trip, and the refusal path, which already costs that read, costs one write more. The refusal changes nothing in the record, so it takes no sequence number and records no Activity, as the idempotency purge does; this adds it to the `WriteBatchNoSeq` line above.
- **A claim's batch also guards that the Task's Claims are those it read: none made since, and none of those open then ended since. Otherwise it is refused, and tried again from a fresh read while the Task is takeable.** Why: the response is built from the read, so a claim whose read saw the holder's Claim live, and whose write ran after the holder released, answered with that Claim `lapsed` at its expiry where the record says `released`. With the guard the response is what the write did, as the Status guard makes it for the Status.
- **The bots work a preset, a Go value in `tools/bots/bot` (`bot.Preset`): Teams with their defaults, Skills, Statuses, Workspaces, agents, human personas and Feature templates with the Steps the planner files. `tools/bots --preset software|accounting` picks one; `software` is the default and is the bots as before (its Teams, Skills, roster and `DefaultPlan`, whose description lines still direct a builder), with no Workspace and the Organisation's own Statuses.** Why: one library serves both the scenario tests and the live load for any trade, and the software preset must keep TestBots as it was (agents-plan R4).
- **`bot.Setup` writes the Statuses only when the preset's list differs from the Organisation's, keeping an existing Status's id where its name matches (ignoring case), else where one of the same kind is left over, and moving the Tasks of a Status it deletes to the first one kept of the same ending; a preset with no Statuses leaves them alone.** Why: run twice it must write nothing, and Backlog becoming Awaiting client or Done becoming Lodged is a rename, not a delete needing `moves`.
- **A preset's Workspace that exists by name keeps its path, and gets its repository back there when the directory is missing; a missing Workspace gets a repository at `<workspace root>/<name>` (`--workspace-root`, default `bots` in `DARKORY_DATA`, else `.dev/bots`, never under `<data>/workspaces/`, which is the Runner's) with one commit on `main`. A directory there with files but no repository is refused. Team defaults are set only when the preset names one and the Team's differs; a preset never turns ship-when-done off.** Why: idempotent by name; a throwaway repository under the dev Install's directory, out of the Runner's way.
- **The bots run git apart from the user's settings (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` set to the null device, the author and committer named after the Member), one write at a time per repository, and not cancelled mid-commit.** Why: a signing key or hook of the user's must not touch a throwaway repository, the e2e harness's HOME has no git identity, and a git killed mid-commit leaves the index locked for the next.
- **A Step may carry what its worker does — the question (aimed at the preset's answering persona unless it names someone), the Skill it is handed over to, the workpaper it appends to and attaches, what a reviewer hands back once and the fix that follows — and a worker reads the Step for a Task of a template before it reads the description's lines.** Why: every Task of a preset has a one-line description for the screens, and the description lines remain for Tasks filed by hand.
- **A worker appends the Step's line to the workpaper in the Task's first Workspace on this machine, commits it with the Task's key, and attaches the whole file; when the Workspace's path is not on this machine it attaches the line alone.** Why: Evidence that is the period's real workpaper, small text, in a repository the Runner can later check out.
- **The accounting drafter has `client-comms` as well as bookkeeping and reconciliation.** Why: the brief gave client-comms only to Mai, and Collect bank statements needs it, yet its question is aimed at Mai, who cannot ask herself; with no other agent able to collect, the drafter does, and Mai keeps client-comms as the client manager (her persona takes only lodgement Tasks and the questions aimed at her).
- **The question Collect raises blocks Collect itself, which the drafter holds while it waits, as every Escalation does; Reconcile is blocked by Collect and waits in Awaiting client, so Mai's answer unblocks it through Collect's completion and Kai's move.** Why: CONTEXT.md's Escalation and the builder's existing path; "completing it unblocks the Reconcile Task" holds through Collect.
- **With `--humans` (on by default) Setup makes the preset's personas and issues each a token, revoked at exit with the bots'; the agents then report to the manager persona (kai, Kai Nguyen), questions are aimed at the answering persona (mai, Mai Tran), and the admin files the Features naming the manager persona as owner. `--humans=false` is the run as before: the admin is asked, owns the Features and ships them with `--ship`. TestBots runs no persona and acts as kai and mai itself.** Why: someone must answer and ship for the live load to keep moving, and `--ask`, `--ship` and the test keep their meaning.
- **A persona claims with a heartbeat timeout and heartbeats while it holds a Task, though a person in the web app claims without one.** Why: a Claim without a timeout is bound to the Member, not the token, so revoking the bots' tokens at exit would leave it held.
- **The owner persona moves a backlog Task to Todo only when it is unblocked and its Feature's Break down has ended, one a round.** Why: the planner files a Task waiting on others into the backlog Status before it sets its blockers; a move in between would make it takeable with its blockers unset, and the planner's block would then fail on a held Task.
- **Accounting completions all rest in Lodged, the preset's one done Status, a Break down and a question as much as a lodgement.** Why: the brief's list has one done Status, and Complete always moves a Task to the first done Status; a Done before Lodged would leave Lodged unreachable.
- **The bots' Notes are one sentence each; the reviewer reads a Task handed over to it as the work, and only a review Task filed for others' work (blocked, never held before) as a review of its blockers.** Why: the screens show Notes in a running log, and the reviewer described the BAS draft as a read of its blocker.
- **A Postgres batch the server ends for a reason of its own is sent again, up to three times in all: a serialization failure (40001), a deadlock it broke (40P01), and "new multixact has more than one updating member" (XX000), which Postgres 14.24 raised once in the two-process soak's `next` when a batch that had updated a Task row aborted at its guard while another held the row's foreign-key lock and a third updated it.** Why: the batch rolls back whole at its Sync, counter and all, so sending it again is the same as having waited for the lock; the alternative was a 500 the client retries blind and an ERROR line in serve.log for a state the record never held. Any other error, a refused guard first, is the caller's to read as before.
- **The accounting preset's Statuses are Backlog and Awaiting client (both of the backlog kind), Todo, In progress, In review, Lodged and Dropped: Backlog is the intake the planner files work ahead into, and Awaiting client a pause for a Task waiting on the client.** Why: with Awaiting client the one backlog Status, every Task filed ahead and every blocked Step waiting for its blockers to be set landed there, reading as waiting on the client when nobody had asked one (UI review 2, #6). The core allows any number of Statuses of a kind; a Task filed without a Status lands in the first todo one, so the planner names the first backlog Status in list order, which makes Backlog the intake. This replaces "Reconcile … waits in Awaiting client" above: it waits in Backlog.
- **The owner persona moves a Task to Todo only from the first backlog Status, never from another such as Awaiting client, and `tools/bots --ship` counts only the first as the Backlog whose leftovers it drops.** Why: a Task in Awaiting client waits on someone outside, and only the person who asked knows when the answer is in; moving it, or dropping it as a leftover, would make it takeable or end it before the client answered.
- **Mai moves the Tasks a question aimed at her blocks to Awaiting client when she first sees the question, the drafter's Claim kept, and back to Todo once she has written the answer, before completing the question; she moves them with the Task status endpoint as a Member of BOOK and TAX. A persona's `Awaiting` names the Status; the software preset sets none.** Why: moving on first sight shows the wait on the board for the 20–60 s she takes to answer at the human pace, not just the moment between her Claim and her Note; moving back while the question still blocks the Task means nothing can take it in between, and the drafter, which completes it as soon as it is unblocked, never races her move. Back to Todo rather than the In progress it came from, because the Claim may have ended meanwhile (a Claim that ends leaves a Task in Awaiting client where it is) and a Task nobody holds must not read as in progress; while the drafter still holds it, it reads Todo until completed.
- **UI review 2's #8 (a Done and a Lodged done Status, lodgements completing into Lodged and the rest into Done) is left undone.** Why: Complete takes only a Note and always moves the Task to the first done Status (`POST /v1/tasks/{task}/complete`; `firstStatusSQL` in the core), and a done Task never moves again, so a Done before Lodged would take every completion and a Done after it none. Choosing the done Status on Complete is a change to /v1 and the core, outside a preset; until then every accounting completion rests in Lodged, as decided above.
- **The Runner merges a work Task's branch when the Task ends Done, whoever completed it: the review's Complete normally, its holder's own Complete the exception. Into the Feature's branch (`feature/<KEY>`), or the default branch for a quick Feature, which ships as before; a conflict works as before. When the completing Claim's Skill is not review (nor a company Skill built on it), the merge Note says so: "Merged <branch> into <target> at <sha> (<workspace>); completed by <agent> under <skill>, without review." (no Skill, no "under"), and a resolving Task's description names the same. A Break down's or a Retrospective's branch is still never merged. In a `pull_request` Workspace the Runner still merges nothing itself, so an unreviewed Task's branch there lands only through a pull request someone opens.** Why: a Feature called done with its work left on a branch is a silent loss, worse than a merge the record shows was unreviewed; the review gate stays the prompt's rule, and the Activity shows who completed (the lead's call, 2026-10-07, after Haiku completed a build Task itself in the check by hand and its quick Feature shipped with the branch unmerged).
- **A build Task's exit rules (a work Task needing a Skill that is not review) no longer offer `complete`: they say to hand it over to review when the builder's part is done, "Never `darkory complete` this Task: it needs the Skill <skill>, and whoever builds a Task hands it over to review; its reviewer completes it, and that merges its branch", or to file a question. A review Task's say to complete it when the work passes ("your Complete merges its branch") or hand it back to the Skill that built it; other Tasks (a Break down, a Retrospective, a Task needing no Skill) keep the three ways. The Feature's line says the branch merges "when the Task is done, after its review".** Why: the old rules offered `complete` "when it is done and no further Skill is needed" to every builder, which a model can read as its own call.

### Filters and Views (2026-10-07)

- **A `filter` token is `field:op:v1,v2…` with each value percent-encoded on its own: the token splits on its first two colons, then on commas, and only then is each value decoded.** Why: a date's offset (`+11:00`) and a search with a comma would otherwise break the grammar, and the query string's own decoding turns a bare `+` into a space.
- **A filter's references are ids and are never looked up: an id that names nothing matches nothing, and a value that is not shaped as an id (a name) is refused `invalid`.** Why: each field is one SQL predicate with no read before it, a View that names a Status removed since still opens, and a name where an id belongs is a mistake worth saying rather than an empty list.
- **`not` and `nin` also match a row with no value for the field** (`skill:not:<id>` keeps the questions, which need no Skill; `aimed_at:nin:…` keeps Tasks aimed at nobody). Why: Linear's "is not" includes the empty ones, and a plain SQL `NOT IN` would drop them without a word; each field's predicate is two-valued, so `NOT` negates it exactly.
- **`kind` is `work`, `breakdown`, `retrospective` or `question`: `question` is a work Task aimed at a Member, `work` a work Task aimed at nobody.** Why: the lead's final vocabulary, shared with the web; the record has no question kind, and a question or an Escalation is filed by aiming a Task at a Member (CONTEXT.md).
- **`claim` is `held` (a live Claim), `unheld` (none, in any state, the same as `holder:is:none`), `lapsed` (a Claim of the Task lapsed within the last 24 hours, the lapse recorded or not, whatever came after) or `session` (the Runner beside this server runs a session for the Task now).** Why: the lead's final vocabulary. A Runner's sessions live in its memory, not the record, so the server passes the ids of the Tasks its attached Runner lists into the query; with no Runner attached (`--runner=off`, or a `darkory runner` elsewhere) nothing is in a session, as `listRunnerSessions` says.
- **There is no `updated_at` field.** Why: a Task keeps no updated time and none is added (the lead's call); the Task date fields are `filed_at` and `completed_at`.
- **`completed_at` is when a Task ended done; a dropped Task has none. `ended_at` on a Feature is when it shipped or dropped.** Why: completing is how a Task ends done (CONTEXT.md); dropping is not completing.
- **`q` matches the key or the title, not the description, as `lower(column) LIKE lower(value)` with LIKE's wildcards escaped, on both engines, so on SQLite only ASCII letters fold case.** Why: the lead's final vocabulary; one predicate for both engines (`ILIKE` is Postgres only); a non-ASCII letter on SQLite matches in its own case only.
- **Dates are RFC 3339 with offset, to the millisecond; `after` and `before` are strict, `gte` and `lte` not, `btw` includes both ends and takes the earlier time first (refused otherwise), and `last` is at or after the server's now less 7, 30 or 90 days of 24 hours.** Why: the lead's final vocabulary; the browser sends a picked local day as its bounds, 00:00:00.000 to 23:59:59.999 at its offset, and times are kept to the millisecond.
- **A list takes at most 50 `filter`s of at most 100 values, each value at most 200 bytes.** Why: keeps each query and its bound arguments small on both engines, well under SQLite's and Postgres' argument limits.
- **`team` is a filter field of both lists, beyond the fields the brief named.** Why: a View of a list across Teams (My work) needs to narrow by Team, and it is one column.
- **`darkory tasks` and `darkory feature list` take `--filter` (repeatable) and the MCP tool `list_tasks` a `filter` list,** passed through unchanged. Why: the generated client already carries the parameter; agents can ask for "unheld, filed this week" in one call.
- **A View is a Member's preference, not the record: saving, changing or deleting one records no Activity (no `view.created`, `view.changed` or `view.deleted`) and takes no sequence number; its write keeps its response under an Idempotency-Key as every write does.** Why: Activity is the trail of changes to the shared record, and one Member's saved filters change nothing anyone else sees; a write that took a number and recorded nothing would leave a gap in Activity. The write runs outside the Organisation's write order (as Heartbeats do), so of two requests under one key at once the second's key fails to insert and it answers with the first's response.
- **Another Member's View is `not_found`, for an admin too.** Why: Views are private preferences; `forbidden` would say one exists.
- **A View's name is unique among its Member's Views of the same list (entity and Team, or across Teams), ignoring case; a taken one is `conflict`.** Why: the bar lists Views by name, and two of one name on one list cannot be told apart. Checked in Go, like Workspace names, since a unique index over a nullable `team_id` treats every null as different.
- **A View's filters are checked by its list's grammar when saved or changed; its `sort` (at most 200 bytes, `""` clears it) and `display` (a JSON object of at most 16 KiB, replaced whole) are kept as the client wrote them and never read by the server.** Why: a saved View always opens as a list the server accepts, while sort and display belong to the web app, which can change their shape without a change to /v1.
- **A View's list (entity and Team) is fixed when it is saved.** Why: its filters were checked against that list's fields; moving it would need them checked again for a list its Member never looked at.
- **The Filter keeps its pills in the address, as `?filter.<entity>=<field>:<op>:<v1>,<v2>`, one parameter per axis, with each value percent-encoded and naming an id, never a name.** Why: a filtered list can then be linked, survives a reload and a rename, and the server's `filter` parameter reads the same tokens.
- ~~**Search on a list is the `q` axis, `q:contains:<words>`, matching the key or the title and ignoring case; it has no parameter of its own.** Why: the server then takes one list of pills, and the chips row draws Search beside the rest.~~ Replaced below (the server's tokens).
- **The Filters menu has no hover flyout; a click, or the arrows and Enter, drills into an axis.** Why: one route serves mouse, keys and touch, and the flyout's pointer-aim machinery was a third of enably's component.
- **One value writes `is` or `not` and several write `in` or `nin`, in both directions; the person chooses only the sign.** Why: Linear's grammar, and a chip never reads "is one of" over a single value.
- **Held by's "Nobody" is the value `none`.** Why: as a value rather than an operator, "Nobody or builder-1" fits in one pill.
- ~~**Kind offers Question for a work Task aimed at a Member by name.** Why: the record has no question kind, and an aimed Task is how a question or an Escalation is filed.~~ Replaced below (the server's tokens).
- **A Status the Filter names with is or is one of is shown even when the Display hides its kind.** Why: "Status is Done" showing nothing because Done is hidden reads as a broken filter.
- **The signed-in Member leads the Member values, marked Me, and the pill names their id, not a "me" that follows the viewer.** Why: the address carries ids, and a shared link should name the same person for everyone who opens it.
- **A date filter's values are RFC 3339 instants with the browser's offset at millisecond precision, a picked local day becoming its bounds (00:00:00.000, 23:59:59.999): after:end(D), before:start(D), gte:start(D), lte:end(D), btw:start(A),end(B) inclusive, last:7d|30d|90d; one picked day is btw of that day.** Why: the server keeps Unix ms and knows no viewer's time zone, so the browser names the instants and both sides compare plainly; dates take no `is`.
- ~~**The Updated filter reads the time the list's Updated column shows: `ended_at` for an ended Task, `waiting_since` otherwise.** Why: the Task record has no `updated_at`, and a filter that disagreed with the column would read as wrong.~~ Replaced below: Updated is not an axis.
- ~~**Claim's values are Held, Unheld (open, nobody holding it), Lapsed (its last Claim lapsed in the past 24 hours) and Live session (a Runner session other than ending works it), as many as hold.** Why: these are the Claim facts the board already shows, and a held Task with a live session is both.~~ Replaced below (the server's tokens).
- **The Feature filter lists the Team's open Features by Rank, then its shipped and dropped ones under their own heading.** Why: the board shows the Tasks of ended Features by default, so they are worth narrowing to.
- ~~**Search on a list is the `q` axis, `q:contains:<words>`, matching the key, the title or the description and ignoring case; it has no parameter of its own.** Why: the server's `filter` reads `q` over all three, and the client-side list must agree with it.~~ Replaced below (the final words, 4868921).
- **Updated is not a filter axis; the Tasks' date axes are Filed and Completed.** Why: the Task record has no updated time, the server's comes from Activity the list cannot see, and a token the web and the server read differently would make a saved View lie.
- ~~**The web's Filter uses the server's words and meanings for every token: Kind `retro` and `question` (aimed at a Member, whatever the kind), Claim `held`, `unheld` (any state), `lapsed_24h` (an expired Claim not yet swept included) and `live_session` (a live Claim with a Heartbeat timeout held by an agent), Blocked as the record's flag.** Why: Views are checked by the server's grammar when saved, and a paged list will pass the same pills to `filter`.~~ Replaced below (the final words, 4868921).
- **The Team pages keep filtering in the browser; their pills pass to `filter=` unchanged when a list needs the server.** Why: they hold every Task and Feature of the Team already, and the tokens are identical.
- **The address names the applied View, as `?view.<entity>=<id>`. The chips row reads its name, adding "edited" once the pills differ from its filters, in any order.** Why: "edited" has to remember which View was applied, and a reload keeps it. An id another Member opens names nothing and is ignored.
- **A Tasks View keeps the Display's order as its `sort`, and the layout, grouping and Show toggles as its `display`. A Features View keeps "Shipped and dropped" as its `display`.** Why: the server keeps both opaque, and these are what each page's Display holds. Applying one sets this browser's Display.
- **Reset leaves the applied View in the same write that clears the pills.** Why: an empty list under a View's name would read "edited" for nothing.
- **Deleting a View asks nothing, and renaming one is a delete and a new save.** Why: as in enably, a View is a preference that takes seconds to remake, and the brief asked for Overwrite and Delete only.
- **The Filter's tokens are the server's as merged at 4868921, words and meanings:**
  - Kind: `retrospective`, and `question` for a work Task aimed at a Member.
  - Claim: `held`; `unheld` in any state; `lapsed` for any Claim of the Task lapsed in the past 24 hours, recorded or only past its expiry, even if the Task was claimed again since; `session` for a Task the Runner runs a session for.
  - Blocked: the record's flag.
  - Search: the key or the title only.

  Why: Views are checked by the server's grammar, a paged list will pass the same pills to `filter`, and the lead's rule is that the web and the server never read a token two ways.

### The Runner at Sacca (2026-10-07)

- **The Runner adds a Task's worktree without a checkout, links the repository's `git-crypt` directory into the worktree's own git directory when the repository has one, and populates the worktree then (`git reset --hard HEAD`).** Why: git-crypt reads its key from `GIT_DIR/git-crypt`, and `git worktree add` gives a linked worktree an empty git directory, so the first real Task at Sacca (enably-v2, whose `secrets/` is git-crypt) failed at the smudge filter before any session could start; the repository's own `scripts/worktree_bootstrap.sh` makes the same link for a person's worktree, through a Claude Code hook that runs too late for the Runner. A link, not a copy, so a rotated key reaches every worktree. The Task's branch is made and recorded in the ledger before the worktree, since the first attempt at Sacca left a branch the ledger did not know, and the next two attempts refused it as "not made by the runner".

### Model v2 (2026-10-07)

The nine decisions are in `model-v2-plan.md`, ADR 0015 and ADR 0016; these are the defaults chosen around them.

- **A new Project starts with the default Workflow** — Backlog (hold) · Plan (breakdown) · Build (engineer) · Review (review) · Retro (retro) · Skill review (skill-review), with the connectors the plan lists — unless its creator picks Copy from another Project or Empty (Backlog → Done). Why: `init`, "+ New Project", the Install checklist and the bots all need a Project that works on first run, and the roster's agents hold exactly these Skills; an accounting Project picks Empty and draws its own. `init` seeds `engineer` and `review` whether or not it seeds the roster, so the default Workflow's steps always have their Skills.
- **No Acceptance step by default, and `acceptance` off on a new Project.** Why: an Acceptance is a second full check of a Parent's whole; a Project that wants one adds the step and switches it on, as Sacca does.
- **Skill review is a step.** A Retrospective's `propose` needs a connector from its step to a step carrying `skill-review`; the proposal is reviewed by advancing the same Task there and published by advancing it into Done. Why: ADR 0010 hands the Retrospective Task itself over to skill-review, and with `tasks.skill_id` gone a step is the only place a Task can wait for a Skill.
- **No migration: the v2 schema is a fresh `0001_init.sql`, 0002–0005 are deleted, and every Install starts from a new database.** Why: the owner said so on 2026-10-07 ("no migration required, just start from scratch new DB"); the only Install that existed is re-created by `init` plus `scripts/sacca-v2.sh`, and a data move from Features and Statuses would have been code nobody runs twice.
- **A Retrospective may carry one pending proposal per Skill, and files follow-up work as top-level Tasks.** Why: MAIN-1's Retrospective found two Skills to change and could file only one, and could not file a follow-up on a shipped Feature.
- **`CLAUDE.md` holds the standard: never weigh implementation cost.** Why: the owner said so on 2026-10-07 after a recommendation that favoured a half-day change over the better model.

Chosen while building M1's record and core rules (M1a):

- **Step, Connector and Label names are unique ignoring case, checked in Go under the write; the exact-spelling unique index on `steps (project_id, name)` and `connectors (from_step_id, name)` stays as a backstop, and Labels have none.** Why: SQLite's `lower()` folds ASCII only, an expression index reads differently on the two engines, and a unique index treats every Organisation Label's null `project_id` as different (as Views and Workspaces already do).
- **A Step's canvas position is whole pixels (`BIGINT`).** Why: the schemas stay comparable on both engines, and a pixel is the canvas's own unit.
- **A Task filed without a Step starts at the first Step whose Skill is not breakdown, acceptance, retro or skill-review — Build on the default Workflow — else the first Step carrying any Skill, else the first Step; with no Steps it is refused `no_step`.** Why: Break down is the switch, never the landing (CONTEXT.md, Workflow, as amended); the first M1a rule, "the first Step that carries a Skill", put every plain Task at Plan, waiting for the planner.
- **`complete` by a holder is advancing along the one Connector into Done (the Claim ends `completed`); a Task aimed at a Member, at no Step, completes as it is, and `advance` on it, with an outcome or without, completes it too.** Why: one way into Done; a question has no Workflow to move through, and an agent ending its work with `advance` should not have to know it held a question.
- **Advancing into Done records `task.completed` with `from`, `outcome` and `since`, not `task.advanced`; `task.advanced`, `task.moved`, `task.dropped` and `task.became_parent` carry `from` and `since` too.** Why: one entry per act, and the time at each Step (`median_ms`) is read from what left it, exactly, since Darkory records when the Task reached it.
- **Advancing into Done a proposal whose base is no longer current sends the Task back along the Step's "needs changes" Connector (else its first Connector to a Step), with the refusal as the reviewer's Note, ends the Claim `advanced`, records `task.advanced` with `refused`, and answers `proposal_stale`, kept under the Idempotency-Key.** Why: the plan's "refused stale, the Task moved back along needs changes with the refusal as its Note"; with no way back, it is only refused, as before.
- **Darkory's own Subtasks — Breakdown, Acceptance, Retrospective — are filed by nobody (`filed_by` null) and recorded with no actor; each names its Parent's Workspaces and has its Owner.** Why: the plan's "filed by nobody"; `filed_by` is now nullable.
- **A Subtask stores `auto_complete` and `acceptance` false, and filing one with either, or with `owner` (`use_parent`), `breakdown` or `from_retrospective`, is refused.** Why: they are a Parent's, and a Subtask has no Subtasks.
- **A Task in an open Blocking cannot take its first Subtask, and a Parent is neither blocker nor blocked (`conflict`); becoming a Parent clears a Task's aim.** Why: "a Parent neither blocks nor is blocked" and "a Parent waits nowhere" (CONTEXT.md).
- **Filing a Subtask takes a Note only when it ends the filer's Claim (a split); otherwise the Note is refused `invalid`.** Why: the Note is the split's hand-off; with no Claim ending there is nothing it explains.
- **`move` is any active Member of the Project or the Owner; a held Task, the Owner or someone above the holder (the Claim ends `taken_back` first, its reason naming the Step), anyone else in the Project or the Owner `held`, anyone else `forbidden`; the mover's Note is written under no Skill before the move; moving a Parent is `conflict`, an ended Task `ended`, the Step it is at changes nothing; a Task aimed at a Member then waits at the Step.** Why: the plan's rule, and the take-back rules of invariant 6; `held` tells someone who could move it once it is free why not now, while a Member outside the Project learns nothing about its Claim.
- **`SetWorkflow` is admins only; `position` places Steps (distinct, from 1, renumbered 1…n) and each Step's Connectors, the order of the lists unread; `x`/`y` left out keep a Step's place, and put a new one at ((position − 1) × 448, 0); Connectors name Steps by id or name, `moves` a deleted Step's id to a Step by id or name; a Connector sent without its id keeps the id of the one out of the same Step with the same name; Tasks carried by `moves` keep their Claims, reach the new Step now, and each records `task.moved` with `workflow_changed`; the reply is the Workflow with its live facts, as GetWorkflow reads it.** Why: a Workflow put back as read is unchanged and writes nothing; editing the Workflow is not a take-back, so a running session goes on; the canvas saves one dragged Step without resending every place.
- **A Step's takers are the active Members of its Project holding its Skill, and for a Step carrying skill-review the Organisation's.** Why: the same Members the Takeable rule offers it to; the plan's "Members of the Project" would show nobody at Skill review where the reviewer is in another Project.
- **Labels: a Project's are defined by any of its Members or an admin, the Organisation's by admins; names 1 to 50 characters, colours `#rrggbb` kept lower-case; any Member of the Project or the Owner sets a Task's Labels, held or not; deleting a Label takes it off its Tasks.** Why: Labels are marks Darkory's rules never read, so the Claim guard does not cover them, and a Project shapes its own vocabulary.
- **The `parent` filter takes `is`, `not`, `in` and `nin` with `none`; `takeable_by` is inclusive (`agents`: some active agent who could take it by its Step's Skill; `both`: an agent and a human); `rank` takes whole numbers with `is`, `not`, `in`, `nin`, `lte` and `gte` over the Rank a Subtask shares with its Parent; `skill` stays as a token, meaning the Step's Skill, and the `skill` query parameter goes; `ended_at` is a date field beside `completed_at`.** Why: one predicate per token as before; `in:agents,humans` and `is:both` then say different things, and "the top ten" is `rank:lte:10`.
- **A new Project's default Workflow makes the generic Skills `engineer` and `review` when the Organisation lacks them; Empty is a Backlog hold with one Connector, "done", into Done.** Why: an Organisation may have renamed or never had them (`init` seeds both), and the default's Steps must carry them.
- **A refusal carries `Details` for programs: `outcomes` (the Step's Connector names, in order) on `no_connector` and `use_advance`, and `proposals` (the stale ones' ids) on `proposal_stale`.** Why: an agent picks an outcome from the record, never by parsing the message.
- **Advancing into Done from Skill review publishes every pending proposal on the Task in one write, or none: when any is stale the Task goes back along "needs changes" with the reasons as the Note, the current ones stay pending, and `details.proposals` names the stale.** Why: a review judges the Retrospective's changes together; publishing half would leave the other half to be reviewed against versions it never saw.
- **`TaskFilter.Step` takes a Step's id alone, or its name only with `Project`; a name without a Project is `invalid`.** Why: names are unique only within a Project's Workflow, and My work lists across Projects.
- **A Subtask filed without `workspaces` names its Parent's, even when its Parent names none; a top-level Task, the Project's default.** Why: its branch starts from the Parent's and merges back.
- **A Label's name is unique across a Project's own Labels and the Organisation's, both ways (`conflict`), and Task bodies name Labels by id or name, any case; a Project Label's Activity carries its `project_id`, which is how the Project's Activity finds it, a deleted one's included.** Why: a name must always mean one Label; a deleted Label leaves no row to join.
- **`CreateProject` takes `copy_from`, `members` (the creator is not added unless named), `default_workspace`, `auto_complete` and `acceptance` in its one write, recording `project.member_added` for each Member.** Why: "+ New Project" sets a Project up in one step, and the admin creating it is often not one of its workers.

Chosen while building M1's `/v1` server, CLI, MCP server, bots and e2e suites (M1b):

- **`CreateProject` answers with the Project and its Members (`ProjectDetail`), read in the same write; a Project's key and name are each taken ignoring case, on create and on rename, compared in Go.** Why: the spec's reply and its "ignoring case"; the core first returned the bare Project and compared names exactly.
- **`workflow show <project> --body` prints the Workflow as the body `workflow set` reads, Steps and Skills by name with the Steps' ids kept; `workflow set --help` documents that body.** Why: GET's shape (`skill_id`, `from_step_id`) is not PUT's, and a person edits names, not ids.
- **The CLI has `label update` beside `label create|list|delete|set`, and finds a Label by name (any case) among the Organisation's and, with `--project`, the Project's own.** Why: every `/v1` operation has a command (invariant 9), and the API names a Label by id.
- **`show` prints the outcomes as `Advance    pass → Review · needs changes → Build`; `tasks` prints the Step, `@member` for an aimed Task, or `parent done/all` for a Parent, then `[in PARENT]` and the Labels.** Why: an agent reads which outcome leads where before choosing one.
- **MCP `list_tasks` returns the Steps of the listed Tasks' Workflows (each with its outcomes) and their Parents' briefs; `show_proposal` returns `{proposals: […]}`, every proposal on a Task or the one by id.** Why: the list reads without a second call, as Statuses did; a Retrospective may carry one proposal per Skill.
- **The Runner's prompt ends a session with `darkory advance <task> <outcome>`, listing the Step's outcomes (into Done marked), or `complete` for a Task at no Step; the nudge says "advance it, complete it, or file a question".** Why: `handover` is gone, and a session told to run it could never end its Task; the rest of the prompt is M3's.
- ~~**Until M3, the Runner reads a Task's Parent where it read its Feature: a Task with neither Parent nor Subtasks stands alone and merges into the default branch; a Parent's Complete merges `feature/<KEY>` as Ship did. A session log that cannot be attached because the next holder already claimed a Task with no Parent is logged as a warning and lost.** Why: the server and CLI changed under it; M3 owns branches, merges and where logs go.~~ Replaced in M3 (below).
- ~~**`darkory init --no-agents` still seeds no Project; init prints Project MAIN when it seeds the roster.** Why: `--no-agents` is documented as "just the Organisation and its first Member"; the web app's checklist starts with "+ New Project".~~ Replaced in M3 (below): init always seeds MAIN.
- **fakeagent's scenarios are `advance` (default; along `FAKEAGENT_OUTCOME` or the one way out) and `complete`; `FAKEAGENT_BREAKDOWN` is `step:title;…`.** Why: Skills no longer travel with a Task; the Step does.
- **The soak runs on a Workflow of Plan, four work Steps A–D (each with "done" into Done and "to-<step>" to every other) and Retro; filers file Tasks with Break down and Subtasks at random Steps and complete their Parents.** Why: it exercises advance, complete, Parents, Breakdowns and Retrospectives under load, and lets the soak check that a Task is at exactly one Step of its own Project or none.
- **The bots' software Workflow gives every Step its own Skill (Backlog hold · Plan · Build · Docs · QA · Review · Triage · Deploy · Retro · Skill review), and the accounting Project is Backlog · Gather · Prepare · Partner review with "lodged" into Done.** Why: a Task's Skill is its Step's, and no-self-review forbids one Member holding a Task under two Skills, so the partner lodges by advancing rather than at a Step of their own.
- **`GET /v1/activity` takes `task` (id or key): the entries whose subject is the Task or, for a Parent, one of its Subtasks (Subtasks filed later included), composing with `project`, `member` and `kind`; an unknown Task is `not_found`. The CLI's `activity --task` sends it. Filtering Tasks by Owner stays the `owner:is:` token.** Why: the Task page's history and stepper read one Task's trail without paging the Organisation's; a Parent's history is its Subtasks' too.

### W0 — marks, the Workflow canvas and the Subtask graph (2026-10-07)

- **`glyphFor` precedence: ended, then Parent, then held, then blocked, then hold, then waiting.** A held-and-blocked Task shows working, since an agent that escalated still holds the Task its question blocks; an agent's live Claim with no Runner session turns as running. Why: the glyph answers "is someone on it" before "can someone take it".
- **Tidy up reads the plan's 240 px as the gap edge to edge**: step nodes are 208×88, so the x pitch is 448 and rows are 128 apart; dagre LR hangs every step from a virtual start, so steps with nothing leading in (Plan, Retro) stand in the first rank; a Connector back into an earlier step lays out as forward; `align UL` keeps chains level. `init`'s default Workflow is stored compact, in the board's order rather than dagre's: Backlog (0, 0), Plan (0, 128), Build (0, 256) · Review (448, 256), Retro (0, 384) · Skill review (448, 384), Done drawn at x 896 — about 1,000 px wide, so a new Project opens with Done in view; one row would have been 2,800 px. Tidy up on it moves steps into dagre's crossing order, which is the cost of a layout that reads top to bottom.
- **Connectors are routed by the canvas's own orthogonal router (`route.ts`), not React Flow's smoothstep.** Why: smoothstep drew lines through nodes and stacked labels where lines met Done. Each outcome's name sits where its line leaves its step; a Connector back leaves by the left and enters from above or below; tests assert no route crosses a node.
- **The Subtask graph's Done and Dropped share one column; worked nodes are not dimmed; aimed Subtasks count as takeable.** Why: the ringed holder is the point of the graph, and CONTEXT.md's Takeable includes a Task aimed at the Member.
- **React Flow's attribution stays.** Why: hiding it is for React Flow Pro subscribers (the library warns otherwise); it is muted, bottom-right.
- **`StatusGlyph` stays until M4 deletes it** (about fifteen screens still draw the Status model `/v1` serves on this branch); `taskGlyph` is `taskWorkGlyph`; the `--agent-border` token is gone in favour of `--agent-gradient`.
- **The design lab at `/dev/design`** (`npm run lab` shoots it) mounts above the sign-in gate only under `import.meta.env.DEV`, lazily, so React Flow is not in the production bundle until a screen uses it.

### The v2 `/v1` spec (2026-10-07)

Defaults taken while writing `api/openapi.yaml` for model v2 (branch `m1-spec`), each where the plan was silent.

- **`createProject.workflow` is an enum (`default | empty | copy`) with `copy_from`**, not a `oneOf`. Why: a union generates clumsy Go for the CLI and server.
- **`PUT …/workflow`: `position` is authoritative (distinct, from 1) and the list order is not read; `x`/`y` are optional — an existing Step keeps its place, a new one lands at `((position − 1) × 448, 0)`; `from`, `to` and `moves` name a Step of the body by id or name; a Connector sent without an id keeps its id when one with the same `from` and name exists; a Workflow may have no Steps (filing is then `no_step`); Tasks moved by `moves` keep their Claims.** Why: PUT keeps GET's shape so a client reads, edits and sends back, and a hand-written `workflow set --file` works.
- **A Task filed without `step` starts at the first Step whose Skill is not breakdown, acceptance, retro or skill-review** (Build in the default Workflow), then the first Step with any Skill, then the first. Why: Break down is the switch, never the landing; the spec's first draft said "first Step with a Skill", which was Plan.
- **A Subtask filed without `workspaces` takes its Parent's.** Why: its branch starts from the Parent's and merges back.
- **Labels: a name is unique across a Project's own Labels and the Organisation's; Task bodies take ids or names; `GET …/projects/{p}/labels` lists the Project's own; `color` (#rrggbb) is required.** Why: a name must always mean one Label, and `label set MAIN-4 bug,client-x` is the CLI.
- **`proposal_stale` stays the code; `Error.details` carries `outcomes` on `no_connector` and `use_advance`, and `proposals` on `proposal_stale`.** Why: an agent picks an outcome from `details`, never by parsing the message.
- **Filters keep `skill` (the Step's Skill), `blocks`, `workspace`, `model`, `rank` (a number field), and have both `completed_at` and `ended_at`; the `skill` query parameter goes; `step` as a query parameter takes a name only with `project`.** Why: My work across Projects needs the Skill, and names are only unique per Project.
- **`Task` carries `skill_id` derived from its Step; `TaskBrief` carries `title`; `filed_by` is absent on Darkory's own filings; `median_ms` names its unit, and durations are otherwise whole seconds.**
- **`fileTask.note` applies to a split (the Note goes on the Parent); `moveTask.note` is the mover's; `createProject.members` does not add the creator unless named; a held Task is moved only by whoever may take it back (Claim ends `taken_back`), anyone else is `held`, which is also the code for filing under a Task another Member holds; `conflict` covers blocking a Parent, making a Parent of a Task with open Blocking, and moving a Parent; `TaskDetail.proposals` is the latest proposal per Skill, oldest first; Activity's `project` filter also covers the Project's Labels; `task.advanced`/`task.moved` payloads carry `from`, `to`, `outcome`, `step_id`, `since` (Unix ms) for the Task page's stepper.**

### M3 — the Runner on model v2, and the API's leftovers (2026-10-08)

- **A Task's branch is `<key>-<slug>` (`main-7-support-emoji`) and a Parent's is `<key>` (`main-7`), both lower case; a Task's branches are found by the prefix `<key>-`, which no Parent's branch and no other Task's carries.** Why: the plan's names; a Parent's branch never matches a Task's prefix, so the ledger and the reuse checks cannot confuse them.
- **A Parent's branch is made from the Parent's own Task branch when the ledger has one (it was worked, then its holder split it), else from the default branch.** Why: what the holder committed before the split is the Parent's work, and would otherwise be stranded on a branch nothing merges.
- **In a pull_request Workspace a new branch starts from `origin/<base>` once fetched (falling back to the local base), and the Parent's branch from `origin/<default>`.** Why: the Subtasks' pull requests merge into the Parent's branch on GitHub, so the local branch lacks them; an Acceptance must start with every Subtask's work.
- **An Acceptance works on its own branch made from its Parent's branch at its tip, as any Subtask, and its branch merges back when it ends Done; a Breakdown's and a Retrospective's never merge.** Why: its checkout holds the Parent's branch with everything merged, as the plan asks, while a fix made after "fail" sends it to Build is reviewed and merged like any other work — committing straight onto the Parent's branch would skip review and leave no head for a pull request in pull_request mode.
- **The ledger's entries carry `Task` or `Parent`; entries from before model v2 carrying `Feature` are read into `Legacy`, kept as written, and matched by nothing.** Why: Sacca's old ledger must still load (the lead's brief); its `feature/` branches are history.
- **A merge's record is a Note on the Task, a Parent's included (the R1 Evidence file `merge-<KEY>.txt` goes).** Why: a Parent is a Task and takes Notes; Features had none, which is all the Evidence was for.
- **In pull_request mode the merge Note names the merged pull request whose head is the Task's branch, or says it is not merged on GitHub yet.** Why: "read the merged pull request carrying the key" (the brief); the person sees which pull request landed it.
- **A merged pull request completes a Task only at a Step carrying review (or a company Skill on it), by advancing along the Step's one Connector into Done; with none or several, a Note asks a person to advance it.** Why: `complete` is refused `use_advance` at a Step like Review with "needs changes" beside "pass", and which way a merge means is unambiguous only when one way leads into Done.
- **A merge that conflicts leaves its Task done: a Note on it with git's report and a Task "Resolve the merge of <branch> into <base>" filed at the Step a session of this runner last committed to the Task's branch at under another Skill than review (its builder's), else the Project's first work Step. Its branch merges into the conflicted Task's base while that base is open: under the Parent, into the Parent's branch; for a Task with no Parent, into the default branch. When the Parent has already ended (the conflicting Subtask's end completed it), it stands alone with the default branch as its base, carrying the conflicted Task's commits there, and "Resolve the merge of <branch> into <default>" is its title.** Why: a Done Task never reopens (CONTEXT.md; `step` refuses an ended Task), so the work goes on in a new Task — option B, approved by the lead on 2026-10-08 with this base rule so no work is lost; an ended Parent takes no new Subtask but questions, and its branch has landed. Claims record a Skill, not a Step, and "builder" is not a Skill (Sacca's QA is neither builder nor review), but the branch tip moving during a session says who built.
- **The Task resolving a merge names the one Workspace the merge did not go into, whatever its Parent's or the Project's default.** Why: its checkout must be the repository holding both branches.
- **A Parent's Complete merges its branch into the default branch even when a done Subtask's work is missing from it (its merge conflicted), and the Note on the Parent names that Subtask and says the merge went without its work, which the resolving Task carries into the default branch.** Why: the lead's rule (2026-10-08); the Parent is done in the record, and the missing work has a Task of its own rather than a branch held back.
- **The three-strikes question is aimed at the agent's manager on its Reporting line, else the Task's Owner; filing it with `blocks` joins the Task's Parent or stands alone, as the core does for every question.** Why: ADR 0013 and the brief; the prompt's `--aim` names the same Member.
- **A session log the record refuses (`not_holder`, the next holder already claimed) is kept on disk in `<data>/sessions/<KEY>/kept/` and attached as the agent whose session it was when the Task is free: when any Claim ends, every Poll, and when a runner starts.** Why: plan invariant 6 takes writes on a held Task from its holder alone, so "never lose it" is met by waiting, not by an exception; the log lands on its own Task rather than the Parent, named for its agent.
- **A quiet session counts as progressing while a process under it that started after its last record (ps's start time to the second) is still there a check later, for as long as it runs; for Claude Code only while its transcript shows a tool call in flight. Failing that, a call in flight counts for up to the Claim's timeout after its last record. The runner's log says which, and when a call outlasts that.** Why: the plan's "progress must survive a long tool call"; the process is the call's own work, a status line's short command is never seen twice, MCP servers started before the call never count, and a call that hangs with no process still lets the Claim lapse, as ADR 0013 wants. "The session log" here is the runner's log for the session, since the pane's log is Evidence kept exactly as the terminal had it.
- **fakeagent's `longcall` scenario: one tool call silent for `FAKEAGENT_CALL` (6m by default), `sleep` as a child process or in the agent (`FAKEAGENT_CALL_IN=agent`), then `advance`.** Why: the plan's six-minute call, shrunk by the timings in tests.
- **The web Activity page's `?about=` names a Task the server resolves: an unknown one is `not_found`, shown as a Refusal rather than "No entries".** Why: the filtering is the server's now (`task`, from m1b-api's cac1219), which resolves references as for `member` and `project`.
- **`taskActivity` reads backwards from the newest entry until a page comes back short; the Activity page reads 100 entries a page with the Task filter too.** Why: one call in practice, complete for a Task of more than 500 entries; the filtering is the server's now.
- **The MCP `activity` tool is unchanged.** Why: it takes no filters at all.
- **`darkory init` always seeds Project MAIN on the default Workflow holding the first Member; `--no-agents` leaves out the roster and the Workspace, and says so. Core `Init` stays bare and seeds MAIN only through `InitOptions.Project`, which `Roster` implies.** Why: the lead's brief (an Install starts with a Project to file into); a Workspace is where agent sessions work; every Go fixture builds its own Projects.


### The Workflow line: since you looked (2026-10-08)

- **A Member keeps one mark per Project of how far they have seen its Activity (`project_seen`, migration 0002; `GET`/`PUT /v1/projects/{project}/seen`): the seq of the newest entry seen, and when it last moved. It only moves forward (a lower or equal seq changes nothing and the response is the mark as kept); a seq past the Organisation's newest entry is `invalid`; 0 is allowed for a Project read before anything happened. Only a Member of the Project has one: anyone else, an admin included, is `forbidden`. Like a View it is a preference, not the record: no Activity, no sequence number, an Idempotency-Key as every write.** Why: the What's happening panel's "since you looked" needs a mark that survives devices and tabs; forward-only means a stale tab never pulls it back; it is a migration rather than a change to 0001 since Installs exist now; the Activity seq is per Organisation, so the mark compares directly with the entries the panel reads.
