- **`ProjectSeen`'s `seq` and `at` are the contract's first `nullable` fields: always present, null until set.** Why: the lead's shape for the web builder; "never looked" is a state the panel reads, not a missing field.
- **A Runner session says since when it is in its state (`RunnerSession.state_since`): its start until the state first changes, then the moment of each change; a repeated state keeps its time, and an ending session keeps the time it began ending.** Why: the panels say "waiting for 4 min", which `started_at` cannot.
- **The Runner records each of its own nudges as `task.nudged` through `POST /v1/tasks/{task}/nudged` `{nudge: 1|2}`, allowed only to the Session holding the Task's Claim (a held write, as a release is), with no actor and the payload `claim_id`, `holder_id`, `nudge`. The payload names the agent `holder_id`, not `member`, as `task.lapsed` does, so the Activity `member` filter finds a Member's nudges. It is recorded after the nudge is typed; a failure to record is logged and the session goes on. The web refreshes nothing for it.** Why: the Runner is a client of the record (plan invariant 9) and holds no server-side handle, so the record needs a write it can call, and only the holder's Session knows a nudge happened; Darkory acted, not the agent, so the entry has no actor, like a lapse; a nudge changes no Task, Claim or session state.
- **An admin's nudge from the session panel (`nudgeRunnerSession`) is not recorded yet.** Why: the lead's brief covered the Runner's own two nudges; recording an admin's (actor the admin, no `nudge` number) is an open question for the lead.
- **`make dev` (and `dev-api`, `dev-web` alone) first stops an earlier run of the same checkout: devrun watchers whose working directory is this checkout, then whatever listens on 7358 and 7357, SIGTERM with 12 s to stop cleanly, then SIGKILL (`scripts/dev-stop.sh`).** Why: the owner restarts `make dev` without finding the old terminal; a leftover run held the ports, and an orphaned devrun kept rebuilding `.dev/bin/darkory` beside the new one.

### Sessions that end (2026-10-08)

- **A token Session ends once no request has come through it for the idle limit, 15 minutes by default (`DARKORY_TOKEN_SESSION_IDLE`, `--token-session-idle`), unless a Claim bound to it is still live. It is part of the one condition `auth.LiveSessionSQL`, so `CallerValid`, `listSessions` and the bearer lookup agree. Replaces "Token Sessions never expire" in the M4 line above.** Why: nothing closed a token Session whose copy stopped without closing it; the owner's Install had 6–8 open per agent hours after the Runners that opened them had stopped, and 33 for its human from one seed run's CLI commands.
- **The limit is three times the Runner's 5-minute Heartbeat timeout.** Why: every Session in use makes a request at least once a minute (a waiting `next` is at most 60 s, a Heartbeat every 30 s, a stream's keep-alive 15 s, and `last_seen_at` moves at most once a minute), so only a Session nothing uses stays quiet that long; a test pins the ratio.
- **A Session holding a live Claim never ends by idleness.** Why: a Claim's heartbeat timeout may be up to 24 hours, and closing a Session ends the Claims bound to it; the Claim lapses on its own rule first, then the Session ends.
- **An idle Session ends at `last_seen_at` plus the limit (`ended_at`), is closed (`closed_at`) by the housekeeping sweep within a second of that, or at once when its id comes back on a request, which then starts a new Session with the same id; the sweep reads before it writes, so a sweep that finds nothing takes no write lock.** Why: every read already treats it as ended, and the unique open (member, chosen id) row must be freed before the id can start again.
- **Ending a Session by idleness records no Activity; closing one (`closeSession`, revoking, deactivating, the Runner's own close) still records `session.closed`.** Why: like starting a Session and touching `last_seen_at` it is presence, not a change to the work record, and no Claim ends with it (a live one keeps it open); recording it would add one entry for every CLI command run without `DARKORY_SESSION`. The brief's "recorded" is met by the row's `closed_at`; the lead may want an Activity entry instead.
- **An Activity stream keeps its Session seen: on each check of its caller it moves `last_seen_at`, at most once a minute.** Why: a stream is authenticated once and was the Runner's reader's only traffic, so it would otherwise end its own Session after the limit.
- **The Runner closes every Session it opened when it stops: each agent's waiting Session as its loop returns, each agent's own Session after the loops end, and the Session of any token it skips.** Why: a stopped Runner left all of them open (defect 1a); the per-Claim close already existed.
- **Two Sessions per agent per Runner start is right, and stays: the agent's own (reading, following Activity for the first agent, and writing as the agent outside a Claim: kept session logs, merge Notes), and the one the next Claim is made in, which the agent's session then works in under the same id (Claude Code's session id) and which is closed when the Claim ends.** Why: a Claim with a timeout is bound to the Session that made it, and `next` both waits and claims, so the Session must exist before the Claim and be fresh for each; the agent's own Session outlives Claims. The agent's own Session of an agent busy on a long Task (not the first agent) goes idle and ends; its next request starts a new one under the same id, so its Sessions list shows an ended row and an open row with one id.
- **`listSessions` takes `state=open|ended` (default open), answers `open` and `ended` counts on every page, and gives each Session `ended_at`; ended Sessions sort most recently ended first. Migration 0004 indexes Sessions by Member for the count.** Why: the web shows "Show ended (N)"; ended Sessions accumulate (one per CLI command without a Session), so the count must not read the whole table.
- **`Copy` (web/src/components/Copy.tsx) keeps 24 px at the end of its value for a 20 px button that shows on hover, on keyboard focus, or anywhere over a row marked `group/copy`; it is hidden by opacity, never removed, so Tab reaches it; a copy turns the icon to a check for 1.5 s with no toast; a refused clipboard toasts the value.** Why: the owner asked for an icon at the end, absolutely placed so nothing moves; a toast for every copy is noise beside the check.
- **One Sessions table (settings/SessionsTable.tsx) serves the agent peek (`compact`: ID · Seen · State, what a Session holds under its id), the Member and agent settings pages and Account (ID · Started · Last seen · State · Holds), and turns compact on a phone. The ID column takes the width left and fits a whole 36-character UUID on one line in both; Last seen reads "40 s ago" with the exact time on hover; ended Sessions sort after the open ones behind "Show ended (N)", 50 a page. An ended Session's Holds is empty.** Why: the owner asked for full ids in a table on both pages; a short id (22) needs no change; a Claim made through an ended Session without a timeout belongs to the Member, not the Session.
- **The Runner's state shows on the Session row whose id is the Runner session's `session_id`: "Open", then the state pill and "since <state_since>".** Why: that Session is the one the agent's session works in (it is Claude Code's session id), so the two meanings of "session" meet on one row instead of contradicting each other.
- **On screen, the Runner's agent session is named by the Runner: the Agents table's column is "Runner" (values: the state pill, host, tmux; "Not running"; "Not run by the Runner") and the peek's section is "Runner". "Session" on these screens means only the glossary's Session.** Why: the glossary has no noun for the agent session; "Shift" is proposed to the lead for it rather than invented on screen.

### Files, and Members' avatars (2026-10-08)

- **The file store is `internal/blob.Store`, the Evidence store's interface (Put of known size, Get, Delete; atomic temp + rename on disk; S3 ready), opened a second time for files: `DARKORY_FILES`/`--files`, default `<data>/files`, or with Evidence in a bucket the same bucket under `<prefix>/files`.** Why: the brief's "Blobs" interface already existed with both implementations; a second abstraction would be two ways to store bytes. A store of its own keeps an avatar's keys apart from Evidence's and lets an Install put files elsewhere; one bucket by default suits Cloud. No `Stat`: size and type live in the `files` row and nothing would call it.
- **`POST /v1/files` takes the raw body with `?name=` and `?purpose=general|avatar`, not multipart.** Why: one upload convention across `/v1` (decision on Evidence above): no multipart parsing, the size is the `Content-Length`, so the store's single streamed `PUT` of known length holds, and the hash is taken on the way; a multipart part has no size, so it would be spooled to disk first. Deviates from the brief's word "multipart".
- **The server reads a file's type from its bytes (`http.DetectContentType`) and keeps only that; the request's `Content-Type` is ignored. Downloads are `inline` only for PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF, else `attachment`; always `nosniff`, `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`, `ETag` of the SHA-256, `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and `If-None-Match` answers 304.** Why: a claimed type is the uploader's word; SVG and HTML can run script, so they never render inline; bytes never change under an id, so a year's private cache is safe and the avatar costs one request per browser.
- **An avatar is uploaded as one (`purpose=avatar`): PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF by its bytes, at most 2 MiB, at most 12000 px a side and 40 MP; the server cuts the middle square, scales it to at most 256 px (CatmullRom, `golang.org/x/image/draw`; WebP decoded by `x/image/webp`) and writes a PNG, renaming the file `.png`. Only such a file can be set as an avatar.** Why: pure Go, so the server resizes and the web needs no canvas code; re-encoding keeps only pixels (no EXIF location, no polyglot tail), which the API says, so nothing is stripped silently; the pixel caps stop a small file decoding to gigabytes. A GIF keeps its first frame, said in the spec.
- **The avatar is `members.avatar_file_id` (migration 0003), set through `PATCH /v1/members/{member}` `avatar_file_id` (`""` removes it, as `default_workspace` does). An admin sets anyone's; a human sets their own, and a request that changes only the avatar is the only one a non-admin may make; an agent's is set by an admin.** Why: the brief's reading; the agent's own token setting its own face was not asked for.
- **Uploading records `file.uploaded` and deleting `file.deleted` (subject type `file`). A file that is a Member's avatar cannot be deleted (`conflict`); changing or removing an avatar deletes the old file in the same write when it was uploaded as an avatar and no other Member shows it. A deleted file keeps its row (`deleted_at`, `deleted_by`) so its id never names other bytes; its bytes are purged after the write (`purged_at`), and a purge that fails is retried after the next deletion in the Organisation.** Why: Activity is every change to the record; refusing the delete keeps no Member's mark broken behind them; releasing the old avatar keeps the store from filling with faces nobody shows, without a sweeper process.
- **A Member who is not an admin may show only an avatar file they uploaded themselves (`forbidden` otherwise), and changing an avatar releases the old file only when the caller could delete it (its uploader, or an admin).** Why: security review: otherwise a human could point their avatar at another Member's pending upload, keep its uploader from deleting it (`conflict`), then release it by changing their avatar, a delete by someone who is neither its uploader nor an admin.
- **Any Member of the file's Organisation reads a file; a file of another Organisation, or a deleted one, is `not_found`. Only its uploader or an admin deletes it. General files are capped at 10 MiB by default (`DARKORY_FILES_MAX_MB`).** Why: the brief; files are the Organisation's, like Evidence, and the id is no secret to hide behind.
- **CSP: `img-src 'self' data: blob:` already allows `/v1/files/{id}/content` and the upload preview's object URL; unchanged.**


### The Workflow editor: a Step list and a Step panel (2026-10-08)

- **Settings › a Project › Workflow is the line on top, then the Steps as a text list beside one Step's panel (Direction C of the editor review board); the list has no fields, the picked Step's name, Skill, takers and outcomes are edited in the panel.** Why: the owner found the row of inputs confusing (who takes a Step, how to remove them, Add Step hard to find); the lead picked C for the room it gives Taken by and for fewer boxes at rest (50 for Main in the old list, 6 in the panel).
- **The picked Step is in the address (`?step=`, replaced, not pushed); with none it is the Step where New Tasks start, else the first. A Step on the line picks it too (`data-step` on the line's Step names).** Why: Edit from the live page already sends `?step=`; replacing keeps Back leaving the editor rather than walking the picks.
- **A new Step is placed, not wired: a hold with no outcome after the Step it was added from, nothing pointed into it; it is listed in that Step's group until its Skill places it (`Draft.placed`).** Why: the lead's call (D9): a new hold read "pass → QA" while Backlog, a hold, read "moved by hand"; wiring is the admin's to say. The old insert re-pointed the previous Step's first outcome into it.
- **Deleting a Step removes every outcome into it from another Step unless the delete dialog leads it to another Step or Done; the dialog asks first whenever the Step holds Tasks, anything leads into it, or it strands a Step. Each removed or re-pointed outcome is counted and listed as a change.** Why: D8: the old `deleteStep` re-pointed a first outcome and dropped the others into the Step without a word, and the header said "1 change" for four; the lead's call is "Remove this outcome" by default, said in the dialog.
- **The header's change count is `describeChanges(...).length`, and the chip lists them (Added, Deleted, Renamed, Skill, Moved, Removed, Re-pointed, Main) with where New Tasks will start when that moves.** Why: one function for the count and the list, so they never disagree; a new Step's outcomes are counted like any other now that a Step is born with none.
- **The main outcome is picked by a radio in the panel (`makeMain`: it becomes position 1, the others keep their order after it); it counts as one change, "Main".** Why: D10: the main way on was only the first by position, changed by removing and re-adding.
- **Taken by offers two acts per Member, each naming its reach before it is made: Take {skill} from {name} (revokeSkill: every Step carrying it in every Project they take it in) and Remove {name} from {Project} (removeProjectMember: every Step there whose Skill they have; not offered for skill-review, taken across the Organisation). Add a Member lists the Project's Members without the Skill, then those not in it, each saying what picking does ("Joins Main, gets engineer", "Gets engineer, here and in Sample"). All act at once, not on Save.** Why: a Step has no assignees; who takes it is the Project's Members with its Skill, so "remove from a Step" is one of these two, and each reaches beyond the Step. No API change: the reach is read from every Project's Workflow and Members and every Member's Skills (`useOrgFacts`).
- **The Owner fallback is said where nobody has the Skill: "Owner takes it" in the list, "Nobody in {Project} has {skill}: each Task's Owner takes it." in the panel.** Why: D7: "No Member has it" was untrue by the Takeable rule.

### Short ids (2026-10-08, ADR 0017)

- **Every id is written as 22 characters of base58 (Bitcoin alphabet), left-padded with `1`; either form is read, forever.** Why: the owner wants ids shown whole; fixed width and an ASCII-ordered alphabet keep UUIDv7's order, and reading the long form keeps every old link and stored id working.
- **Storage keeps canonical UUIDs; the conversion is at the API's boundary only.** Why: the owner's Install has real data, and a boundary change is reversible where a migration is not.
- **`format: id` in the spec, mapped to `shortid.ID` in the server's generated types only (type-mapping in `internal/server/gen/oapi-codegen.yaml`); the Go client keeps strings.** Why: the compiler then finds every id the server writes, and the Apache-2.0 client must not import the AGPL codec (ADR 0009); a client passes ids through.
- **A spec test fails when a property named `id`, `*_id`, `*_ids` (or `labels`, `filed_by`, `published_by`, `attached_by`, `created_by`) lacks `format: id`, except the references that take an id or a name.** Why: a new id field cannot forget the format.
- **A refusal's message has every UUID in it written short.** Why: a message echoes ids ("no Label …"); it names them as the rest of the reply does.
- **Activity payloads and Error details are rewritten by one walk: every UUID-spelled string at any depth and as a map key, except under free-text keys (`title`, `name`, `body`, `env`, `args`, `outcome`, …).** Why: payloads are free-form; a key allowlist rots as kinds are added, while a free-text key list fails safe.
- **References resolve as `id = canonical OR natural key = as given`.** Why: a name that happens to be 22 base58 characters still resolves by name; looksLikeID now refuses new names spelled as either form.
- **The `Darkory-Session` header is canonicalised; a Session's chosen id is written short when it is a UUID; the CLI's keeper compares Session ids by canonical text.** Why: one Session whichever form a copy sends, and a keeper that recognises its own Claims.
- **A browser Session's chosen id is its own id, no longer `browser-<UUID>`.** Why: so it shows short like any id; its `kind` says it is a browser's. Those made before keep their name until they end.
- **View filters are stored with canonical ids and written with short ones (`core.FilterIDs`).** Why: storage keeps one form; the web compares a View's values with ids from the API.
- **The Runner hands Claude Code `shortid.Canonical(session)` for `{session_id}` and finds the transcript by it; it compares a kept log's Member id by canonical text; the server compares Runner session Task ids by canonical text.** Why: those edges need or hold the UUID; the Runner reads ids from the API, now short.
- **The web shows ids as the API gives them, whole, in mono with Copy; `shortSessionId` is gone; on a phone the Sessions table puts the state under the id so 22 characters stay on one line. Search parameters that carry ids (`?step=`, `?scope=`, `?member=`, `?about=`) read a long id as its short form (`web/src/lib/shortid.ts`).** Why: the owner's ask; old links keep working.


### The software Workflow (2026-10-08)

- **A design is a work Subtask (`Design: …`) at a Design Step, never the Breakdown's own work.** Why: the Runner merges only work and Acceptance branches (`merged` in `internal/runner/merge.go`), so a design document written in a Breakdown would never reach the Parent's branch; a work Subtask's branch merges into it on `approved`, before the slices branch from it.
- **The architect blocks every slice by the Design Subtask.** Why: a slice must not start before its design is approved, and must branch from a Parent branch that already holds the design.
- **Plan and Triage belong to product, not to the architect.** Why: they set the definition of done and choose the path; the architect designs. Triage's design path is a split (a `Design: …` Subtask filed under the held Task), since a held Task cannot be turned into a Break down and a design on the Task's own branch would be stranded when it became a Parent.
- **Release is a Step before Done for every Task, and an Acceptance goes on to it (`pass` → Release).** Why: merging is the release (a Parent's merge into the default branch is the deploy trigger), so the last gate is before the merge; a Parent is at no Step, and its Acceptance is the one Subtask that carries the whole Parent's branch.
- **Security review is chosen by the code reviewer (`security review` vs `pass`), not by a rule.** Why: one Skill per Step and Labels are read by no rule; the reviewer reads the `security` Label and the diff.
- **Each role is a generic Skill on its Step plus a company `software-<role>` Skill held by its agent.** Why: takeability reads the Step's Skill, the prompt puts the company text first, and only a company Skill can take a Retrospective's proposal.
- **setup.sh keeps Step ids by name on a re-run and moves Tasks at Steps the preset no longer has to Backlog.** Why: `workflow set` treats a Step without an id as new and refuses to delete one with Tasks; a re-run must never strand work.
- **The proof's Install keeps its data in the scratchpad, not under the worktree.** Why: sessions run in `<data>/workspaces/…`, and Claude Code reads every `CLAUDE.md` from the working directory up; under a Darkory checkout the agents would read Darkory's own rules. Sacca's `.dev` under `darkory/` has the same exposure.
- ~~**A Task completed at a Step after its review merges as reviewed when its last review Claim ended by advancing or completing and no commit on its branch is later than that; a later commit is named ("its branch changed after <reviewer>'s review"); none at all stays "without review".** Why: the run's fast-path Task was reviewed at Code review and released by devops, and its merge said "without review". Commit times are whole seconds, so a commit in the very second a review ends counts as reviewed; a real session starts seconds after the Claim it follows.~~ Replaced below: commit times are the committer's to choose.
- **A Task branch an earlier session left is brought up to its base when a session prepares it again: moved to the base when it has no commits of its own, the base merged into it (`--no-ff`, in the checkout) when it has, and left as it was when that merge conflicts, with a warning in the Runner's log; the conflict then meets the Task's own merge.** Why: in the run, LS-7 was taken before it was blocked, released on a question, and its branch stayed on the Parent's branch as it was then, without the design, the health check or the slice it builds on.
- **A Subtask's session waits, at most 30 seconds, before preparing its checkout until every done sibling's branch (work or Acceptance) is in the Parent's branch, in each plain Workspace, unless the merger already tried that merge (a conflict is not waited for).** Why: in the run, LS-8 became takeable when LS-7 ended and was branched 0.3 s before the merger merged LS-7 into the Parent's branch; its review found the conflict and sent it back. The Parent's done Subtasks come with the Parent (`ParentInfo.Done`), and the merger records each Task it tried.
- **A completed Parent whose branch conflicts with the default branch files a Task standing alone in its Project, "Resolve the merge of <parent branch> into <default>", in the Workspace that conflicted, as a Subtask's conflicting merge does; the Parent stays done and its Note names the Task.** Why: in the run, LS-1 auto-completed after its Acceptance and Release, and its merge into main conflicted with the fast-path Task merged there meanwhile; the Runner only wrote "merge it by hand", so a done Parent's work sat outside main with nobody asked to land it.
- **Reviewed work is attested by content: as a review session starts, before its agent runs, the Runner writes a Note by the reviewer, "Reviewing <branch> at <sha> in <Workspace>.", for each checkout. A Task completed at a later Step merges as reviewed only when its branch tip, read under the repository lock and unchanged through the merge, is the SHA in the first such Note the last review Claim's holder wrote during that Claim; otherwise the Note says "its branch changed after <reviewer>'s review", "nothing records the commit <reviewer>'s review saw", "its branch could not be read to check it against <reviewer>'s review" when the tip cannot be read, or "<reviewer> reviewed work it had built itself" when the reviewer also held the Task under another Skill.** Why: security review of f4e269a: a commit's time is the committer's to set (GIT_COMMITTER_DATE, amend, rebase), so a later Step could backdate new code past the review. The reviewer's own commits during review come after the attested commit and so are not reviewed work. The attestation lives in the record, by the reviewer's Member, written before the agent can write anything.
- **A command group named alone (`darkory label`, `darkory workflow --help`, `darkory label sett`) lists the group's commands with their arguments, exit 2 (exit 0 with --help), instead of "unknown command".** Why: in the second proof run an agent ran `darkory label`, read `unknown command "label"`, concluded the CLI has no `label set`, and its Retrospective wrote that into a Skill proposal; the command was there all along.
- **The commit a review saw is recorded when the review session starts, not when its Claim ends.** Why: at the end, the next holder's session can claim and commit before the ending session records anything (seen in the test: devops started 4 ms after the review advanced), and a Note by the reviewer is refused once another Member holds the Task. At the start the Runner holds the reviewer's Claim, the agent has not run, and the tip is exactly what the review is shown; whatever lands later, the reviewer's own commits included, is after it.
- **`file` takes `blocked_by` (CLI `--blocked-by KEY[,KEY]`, MCP `file_task.blocked_by`): the Task is blocked by each in the filing's own write, with a `task.blocker_added` per blocker, so it is never takeable before they end. A blocker may be in any Project of the Organisation, never a Parent; Break down refuses it (a Parent is never blocked); a blocker the new Task itself blocks, directly or through others, is refused `cycle`. Only the filing needs the authority to file; blocking a Task one files needs nothing more.** Why: the lead's decision (a) of 2026-10-09; in the first proof run a slice filed then blocked was claimed in the second between the two writes and built without its design.
- **A Task aimed at a Member (a question, an Escalation, the three-strikes question) gets no checkout and no branch, and its completion merges nothing; its answer lives in its Notes. A Task moved from its Member to a Step is worked as any other.** Why: the lead's decision (c) of 2026-10-09; in the first proof run the architect's answer to LS-10 committed a toolchain bump on the question's branch, which merged into the Parent's branch past every review.
- **An agent paused while `next` waits, or while its session is prepared, starts no command: the Runner reads the agent's settings again when `next` returns a Task and once more just before it starts the command, and when paused releases the Task unworked with the Note "The agent was paused while it waited for this Task, so the runner released it without starting a session."** Why: in the first proof run a reviewer session started after `--paused` landed, its `next` already in flight.
- **The Runner's Task directories have a root of their own, `--workspaces` / `DARKORY_WORKSPACES` on `serve` and `runner`: by default `<data>/workspaces` as before, but `~/.darkory/workspaces/<data's name>-<first 8 hex of sha256 of its absolute path>` when the data directory is inside a git checkout or under a directory holding a `CLAUDE.md`. A Task whose checkouts an earlier Runner made under `<data>/workspaces` (its `checkouts.json` there) keeps working there until it ends; the ledger of branches and the sessions stay in the data directory. The Runner logs the root at start.** Why: Claude Code reads every `CLAUDE.md` from a session's working directory up to the root, so Sacca's agents, working under `darkory/.dev`, read Darkory's own rules. Keyed by the data directory's path rather than the Organisation's id, which the Runner learns only once it has connected, after it has planned where checkouts go; Local holds one Organisation per data directory.
- **A Project stores its colour (`color`, 0–11, an index into twelve hues 30° apart); a new one takes the hue farthest from those its Organisation's Projects have, the lowest on a tie, unless its creator names one, and migration 0005 colours the Projects already there in creation order by the same rule (ADR 0018). The API spells it `color`, as a Label's is. The theme sets only the mark's lightness and strength (`--mark-l`, `--mark-c`); the chart tokens stay for charts.** Why: a hash of the key into the chart tokens changed hue with the theme and put Big, Sample and Software on one orange; a hash into twelve hues still collides for two of four Projects about 43% of the time, and only the Organisation knows which hues are taken.
- **One duration format in the web app: "40s", "12m", "1h 2m" under ten hours, "18h", "3d", from `durationText` in `lib/time`; a span that ended reads at least "1s".** Why: two styles had grown ("40 s", "12 min" beside "40s", "12m"), and a Parent's stay under half a second read "Triage 0 s".
- **Review Steps stay one after another (Code review → Security review → QA): no Step carries several Skills and no Task stands at two Steps.** Why: the lead's decision (b) of 2026-10-09; written up in docs/workflows/software.md as a known limit.
- **A Parent's branch is not refreshed from the default branch automatically: devops checks at an Acceptance's Release that it still merges (`git merge-tree`), and a completed Parent whose merge conflicts files a Task to resolve it (367d699).** Why: the lead's decision (d) of 2026-10-09; an automatic refresh would land merges no review saw.
- **A branch Step's name line on the Workflow line counts its tokens' halo (`TOKEN_HALO`, 6 px: the "now", selected and ringed box-shadows in globals.css) in its box, stands 48 px over its station (was 38), with rows 66 px apart (was 56), the "Break down" note above Plan's halo, and the first row 64 px under "After a Parent".** Why: at 1440 a picked-up Retrospective's "now" halo covered the row's "propose" and "publish", which the no-overlap tests could not see because the box stopped at the token's edge.
- **The Runner's agent session is a Shift (CONTEXT.md): every word on screen, in the CLI's help and output, in the Notes the Runner writes, its log and the agent's prompt says Shift (the Agents table's column and the agent's peek section included, which named it "Runner"); "Session" stays the glossary's Session, which a Shift works under. The CLI's `darkory sessions [nudge|stop]` is `darkory shifts [nudge|stop]`, the old names kept as unlisted aliases; a Shift's log is Evidence named `shift-<KEY>-<agent>-<HHMMSS>.log`; the Runner counts its silent releases by "Shift ended without a decision" and by the older "Session ended…". API paths (`/v1/runner/sessions`), JSON fields, the data directory's `sessions/` folder, tmux's sessions and Go and TypeScript names are unchanged.** Why: the owner approved Shift on 2026-10-09; "session" named two things on one screen (an agent's Sessions table beside its runner session), and renaming the wire and the disk would break the owner's Install and scripts for no gain to anyone reading a screen. Supersedes the line above that named it by the Runner for want of a word.
- **`PUT …/workflow` also carries who takes the Steps: `skills` (new generic Skills, created first so a Step or a grant names one), `joins`, `grants` and `revokes`, all in the Workflow's one write; refused, none of it is made. The editor's Taken by edits the draft and Save sends them with the Workflow.** Why: the editor is one draft saved whole, and Taken by acting at once beside it needed a sentence ("changes here happen at once, not on Save") to explain itself; one write leaves no half-saved state to explain either.
- **Remove on a Step's Taken by takes the Step's Skill from the Member; it asks first only when that reaches past this Step (another Step here with the Skill, or another Project). Removing a Member from the Project is the Members page's act, not the Step's.** Why: a Step is taken by the Project's Members with its Skill, so its Skill is the one thing a Step owns about who takes it; the owner asked for one plain Remove (2026-10-09).
- **An agent's mark rings in the full-strength AI gradient about an eighth of its width across (2.5 px at 20, 3.5 px at 28, 5 px at 40, 12 px in the 96 px Avatar preview), with a clear 1 px gap between ring and face; the ring is drawn by ::before over the mark's edge and the face shrinks inside it, so the box is the human's. A human's mark has only a neutral hairline. A live Claim changes how the ring is drawn (turning, or a flat amber, red, grey; a human's a still 2 px ring), never its width.** Why: the owner asked for agents to be easy to tell at a glance (2026-10-09), and the lead found 2 px only slightly thicker than before at table size; the gap makes the ring read as a ring, not a coloured edge, and is clear rather than painted so it holds on any row, card or stack.
- **One ⓘ explains a field: `InfoTip` beside its label opens on hover and keyboard focus and pins on a click or a tap (touch), named "About <label>", floating so nothing moves; forms take it as `info` (`FormRow`, `SettingsRow`, the dialogs' `Field`). A line under a field is only an error, a status or a destructive warning; "optional" goes, as a field is optional unless marked; a settings card's line that only listed its rows goes. `InfoPopover` is gone; `Tip` stays as a control's hover word (Remove).** Why: the owner's rule of 2026-10-09, "less descriptive, but intuitive": short labels and icons, no explanatory sub-lines.
- **File a Task in groups, each a decision the filer makes: the Task (Title, Description, Labels); Belongs to (Project, Parent, Owner, which a Subtask takes from its Parent); Start (Step, Blocked by, Workspaces); Subtasks (Break down, Auto-complete, Acceptance) for a Task that may become a Parent; Question behind its switch, on when the entry point names one. No "In MAIN." under the title, no "Starts at Build" by the buttons. Auto-complete and Acceptance stay offered without Break down; for a Subtask or a question they are not sent, so the Project's defaults apply.** Why: the owner asked for logical groups (2026-10-09); a Task's `auto_complete` and `acceptance` cannot be changed after filing, and any Member may file a Subtask under it later, so hiding them behind Break down would take the decision away from every Task broken down by hand.
- **File a Task offers Blocked by (`blocked_by` on file), hidden while Break down is on.** Why: the API takes it in the filing's one write, so the Task is never takeable before its blockers end; a Parent is never blocked.
- **A Project has one or more named Workflows: a Step belongs to one, Step names stay unique per Project, a Connector may lead into a Step of another Workflow of the same Project, and a Task's Workflow is that of its Step, never stored (ADR 0019).** Why: the owner wants a bug flow, a prototype flow and a support flow each seen alone; a board of every Step does not read, a View is one Member's own so it cannot be the shared answer, and a Workflow chosen by a Task's kind is the layering ADR 0016 refused. Nothing is built yet; the editor, board, CLI and API changes follow.

### Named Workflows (2026-10-09, ADR 0019)

- **The write stays the Project's whole graph: `PUT …/workflow` takes `workflows` and every Step with its `workflow`; the editor edits one Workflow and saves whole.** Why: a crossing Connector and the Step it reaches must land in one write, and a Workflow saved alone could not say where its Tasks go when it is deleted.
- **A Workflow has a `position`; a Project's Steps are ordered by Workflow position, then Step position. "The first Step" (a filed Task's default entry) and the first Step carrying `breakdown`, `acceptance` or `retro` read that order.** Why: no new fact; the order the admin sees on the rail is the order the record reads.
- **A Workflow sent without an `id` keeps the id of the Workflow with the same name, ignoring case; any other is new.** Why: as a Connector does; a preset re-run must never delete and recreate a Workflow, which would strand its Steps' Tasks.
- **Migration 0006 names every existing Workflow "Work"; `default` and `empty` Projects start with one Workflow named "Work"; the software preset's is "Software".** Why: a Project's work; the name shows only when a Project has two or more.
- **An ended Task keeps `last_step_id`, the Step it ended at, set in the same UPDATE that ends it; `moves` re-point it when its Step is deleted, and otherwise the FK sets it null.** Why: a Done card belongs on the board of the Workflow it ended in; the Stepper already says "A Step since removed".
- **A Parent shows on the board of the Workflow that owns its least-advanced Subtask's Step.** Why: `placeOf` already puts it there; a Parent is at no Step.
- **Where a Task is listed is the server's, read in `workflow_id` by one rule (`workflowOfSQL`): the Workflow of its Step or of the Step it ended at; an open Parent's least-advanced open Subtask at a Step (Workflow position, then Step position), else the Subtask that ended last; an ended Parent's Subtask that ended last at or before it, ties least advanced first; a Task aimed at a Member, while open, by the first open Task it blocks at a Step (Workflow position, then Step position: a question blocking Tasks in several Workflows is listed with the least advanced), else by its Parent; absent when none gives one. `listTasks`' `workflow` and the `workflow` filter read the same expression.** Why: the board, the Workflow page, `tasks --workflow` and MCP's `list_tasks` then place every Task alike, with no per-Parent reads in the client; a Retrospective ended after its Parent does not move it.
- **Migration 0007 replaces `tasks_parent (parent_id, state)` with `tasks_org_parent (org_id, parent_id, state)`.** Why: SQLite keeps no statistics, and with the Parent alone leading it read a Parent's open Subtasks through `tasks_open_step`, every open Task of the Organisation, once per Parent on every list (and in the auto-complete check); with `org_id` leading it matches all three terms on both engines, and a write keeps one index as before.
- **Step names stay unique per Project; Workflow names are unique per Project, ignoring case, 1–50 characters, never spelled as an id.** Why: a Step name must mean one place in `--step`, `move` and the filters.
- **The board and the Workflow page show one Workflow at a time, picked by a chip in the breadcrumb (`?workflow=`, read long or short, the first by position until one is picked, then remembered per Project in the browser; hidden with one Workflow); the Tasks list stays the whole Project and prefixes each Step group with its Workflow when there are two or more.** Why: the owner wants a flow seen alone; the list is where everything is.
- **On the line, a Connector into another Workflow is an exit chip `outcome → Workflow › Step`, and the Step it reaches carries an entry mark `from Workflow · outcome`.** Why: ADR 0019's Consequences; the line must never drop a Connector silently.
- **The CLI's `workflow show` prints a heading per Workflow only when the Project has two or more, and a crossing outcome as `bug → Bugs › Investigate`.** Why: one Workflow needs no heading; the target's Workflow is what the reader needs.
- **A migrated Workflow's id is a UUIDv7 whose time part is its Project's `created_at`.** Why: invariant 3 says ids are UUIDv7, and a Project's Workflow is as old as the Project.
- **`tasks.last_step_id` is indexed where not null.** Why: the FK's SET NULL and `moves` look Tasks up by it.
- **A `position` left out or 0 reads as the item's place in its list; only a negative one is refused.** Why: a hand-written `workflow set` body lists its Steps in order and should not have to number them; the spec said so for Steps already, and now says it for Workflows and Connectors.
- **`workflow show --body` refuses `--workflow`.** Why: a partial body cannot be sent back to `workflow set`, which takes the Project's whole graph.
- **`workflow show --json` with `--workflow` prints the narrowed body: that Workflow, its Steps and the Connectors out of them, whose `to_step_id` names a Step of the whole Project, so a crossing Connector's leads outside the narrowed `steps`; a client reads the full body for its name.** Why: as `labelsOf` does, `--json` prints in the server's schema the Workflow the text shows, and the text itself reads the whole Project's to name a crossing's target.
- **The software preset's `setup.sh` owns one Workflow, Software, and carries every other Workflow of the Project across with its ids, Steps and Connectors; Software takes the id of the Project's only Workflow, else the one named Software (ignoring case), else the one holding the most of the preset's Step names (the first on a tie), else none, and comes first; before it writes anything it refuses a Project where another Workflow has a Step named as one of the preset's, naming each `<Workflow> › <Step>`; a current Connector out of a preset Step into another Workflow is kept after the preset's, unless it shares its name with a preset outcome out of that Step, which replaces it with a line on standard error.** Why: the body is the Project's whole graph, so a body with Software alone deleted every other Workflow and moved its Tasks to Backlog; the name comes before the Steps, unlike the bots', because naming a Workflow Software is the operator's way to choose it when a clash is refused; refusing at the end left Skills, agents, tokens and Labels written for a Project the preset could not take; refusing a same-named crossing would block a re-run after the operator renamed an outcome to the preset's, so it is replaced, loudly.
- **The bots bind wanted Workflows to the Project's by scoring every (want, have) pair by the Steps they share by name, then by a name match, both ignoring case, and taking the binding with the most shared Steps in all, then the most name matches, no two wanted sharing one; the Project's only Workflow binds the only one wanted; `stepFor` looks only in the hold Step's Workflow.** Why: binding by name alone deleted and remade a renamed Workflow, and binding each wanted Workflow in turn to its best let an earlier one take the only Workflow a later one could have; a Task's Workflow is that of its Step (ADR 0019).
- **`workflow show --json` with `--workflow` prints the narrowed body: that Workflow, its Steps and the Connectors out of them.** Why: as `labelsOf` does, `--json` prints in the server's schema what the text shows.
- **The line takes the Project's whole graph and the Workflow it draws (`LineWorkflow.drawn`; unsaid, the first of several, or every Step of a Project's one), not the drawn Steps alone; where New Tasks start and which Steps leave the line are read from the whole graph, then kept where drawn. An exit is a chip at the end of a short leg down from its Step, a plain chip under everything where that leg would cross a line; an entry is the arrow into the line's first Step when New Tasks do not start there, else a mark over its Step's head.** Why: an exit names a Step the drawing does not have (`bug → Bugs › Investigate`), and Investigate alone would read as where New Tasks start.
- **A Step off the main line (on the branch "After a Parent", or the breakdown Step) carries its exits and entries as chips beside its station, on the line and down a phone; every crossing has a square-cornered route through its chip; a mark that wraps breaks after its "·" or not at all. A parked hold never carries one: a Connector into or out of it, from any Workflow, keeps it on the line.** Why: the line never drops a Connector, and a drawing-level test now holds every fixture and each of the five Workflows to it at every width from 440 px.
- **The Workflow page reads the chip's pick as the board does (`?workflow=`, shared and remembered), its crumbs Project › Workflow chip › Workflow › scope; the chip shows at every width on both pages.** Why: one pick for both views of a Workflow, and on a phone the chip is the only way to another.
- **On the Workflow page of one Workflow of several, the line's hidden count, Needs you, What's happening, the Text view and the Blocking view hold the Tasks that Workflow's board shows, each where the server lists it (`listedOn`, its `workflow_id`), read off the Tasks the page reads: the open ones, those done today and the ended Parents of open Subtasks; with no Workflow from the server, an open Task is on every page and an ended one on the first. Another Workflow's Tasks join the Blocking only as outside Tasks; the "N today" under Done counts the Tasks listed in the Workflow drawn. The scope menu keeps line membership at every Workflow count: a Parent is offered on each line one of its open Subtasks is on, wherever the Parent is listed (an ended one beside its open Retrospective, named by its key and title). A pick of another Workflow drops `?scope=` when the Task scoped to is not listed there, and a Parent's when it is neither listed there nor has an open Subtask on that line.** Why: the page and the board agree, so a Parent has one place to look for it; with the server placing every Task, the line reads no whole list and draws as soon as the open Tasks are read; What's happening still reads the Project's Tasks to word its entries; the scope menu narrows the line, so it offers what is on the line.
- **A Project of one Workflow draws every Step, its one Workflow picked or not (`drawnWorkflow` is none under two).** Why: one path for a one-Workflow Project whoever passes a Workflow (the page, a Task's line), the one the pinned layouts hold.
- **A Task advancing along a crossing Connector travels its exit chip's route off the line, or its entry's onto it; moved by hand into another Workflow's Step it drops straight down off the line, moved in from one it appears at its Step.** Why: the line shows where it went without drawing a Step it does not have.
- **A Parent's Subtask line draws the Workflow its open Subtasks share, else that of the first in the Project's order; the open Subtasks at other Workflows' Steps are counted in the Subtasks header, "· 2 in Support", not on an exit chip.** Why: the header has a place for every Workflow, while an exit chip exists only where a Connector leads; a Subtask never vanishes silently.
- **A Task aimed at a Member shows on the board of the Workflow of the Task it blocks, else every Workflow's board while open and the first Workflow's Done once ended.** Why: a question has no Step; where it matters is beside the Task it holds up.
- **The Task it blocks is read off the other Tasks' `open_blockers` (a Task carries no `blocks`); blocking none, a Subtask aimed at a Member shows on its Parent's board, and once ended lands in its Parent's Workflow's Done.** Why: a question under a Parent is about that Parent's work, and an ended one blocks nothing any more.
- **An ended Parent counts only the Subtasks that ended at or before it did, and Subtasks ended together go to the least advanced in the Project's order.** Why: the Retrospective is filed when the Parent ends and would drag its Done card onto the retro Step's Workflow; a cascade drop ends every Subtask at one instant and the Parent should stay on the board it was on.
- **The editor edits one Workflow at a time: a rail of the Workflows above the Step list, shown to an admin even with one (its `+ Workflow` is the way to a second), to anyone else only with two or more. A pick there is replaced in the address, as `?step=` is, and clears the picked Step; with no `?workflow=`, a `?step=` opens its own Workflow.** Why: Back leaves the editor rather than walking the picks, and Edit from a Step on the live page lands beside it.
- **A Workflow made in the draft is sent without an id and named by its Steps; it is not remembered as the browser's pick until saved, and Save opens the live page on it by the id `/v1` gave it.** Why: the record knows it by name until then; a draft id remembered would be passed over on the next page.
- **A Step moved into another Workflow from its panel goes last there, and both Workflows are numbered again; it is one change, "Moved Fix to Support", never also a move within a Workflow.** Why: its place among its new neighbours is the admin's to say with the list's order, as for a new Step.
- **Where New Tasks start, when the draft moves it (a Workflow reordered, a Step deleted or given another Skill), is said under the change list, not counted as a change.** Why: it follows from the changes; the count stays `describeChanges(...).length`.
- **Deleting a Workflow is deleting each of its Steps: each change (the Workflow, every Step, every outcome into it removed or led on) is counted and listed, and the last Workflow is not deleted.** Why: one rule for what a delete does, and the count never hides a removed outcome.
- **Advance names where an outcome leads only when it crosses: the split button and its caret read `Advance · bug → Bugs › Investigate`, and `Advance · pass` within the Task's Workflow as before; the dialog and its toast name every target (`Waits at Bugs › Investigate`, `Waits at Fix`, `ends Done`). Move's Step picker groups Steps under their Workflows, the Task's own first.** Why: the crossing is the surprise worth a word on the button; a Step of its own Workflow says enough by its outcome, and the dialog is where the reader looks before committing.
- **A Task's path names the Workflow it crossed into (`Bugs ›`) before that Workflow's first Step; its line draws the Workflow it is in and lights the entry it came in by (`from Triage · bug`), the only entry shown down a phone.** Why: the path is where a reader follows a Task across Workflows, and the line has no Step of the one it left to draw.
- **The Agents table and an agent's peek name each Step it takes as `Workflow › Step` when the Project has two or more, in the Project's order; so does a list row's Step pill.** Why: Step names alone no longer say where in the Project a Step is.
- **On a phone the Workflow chip keeps its own width (a crumb `whole`): a short name never truncates, and a long one is cut at about 12 characters before its caret. The Project crumb gives it its room: its name and its "/" hide, and its mark stays at about 20 px, linking to the Project as the crumb did (the board's, its own page, is no link). Beside the chip the board's Views, Filter and Display fold into one menu ("More", its items opening each under it; F still opens Filters; it carries the Filter count, in its badge and its name, "More, 2 Filters set", as its Filter item does, "Filter, 2 set"), and the List | Board switch into a menu under the layout's icon (its check mark first); with no chip, and from `sm` up, they are the buttons and the two icons. The Workflow page's own name crumb steps aside while the chip shows.** Why: at 390 px the bar squeezed the chip to "Bu" with no caret; with the mark beside it, three action buttons left "Features" at "Feat…"; on a phone the chip is the only way to another Workflow, and the mark keeps the bar saying which Project it is; with no chip everything fits and the buttons save a tap.
- **A Task moved by hand (`useMoveTask`) has the Project's Task lists read again once the move lands; the Workflow page's scoped Task detail only fills a gap in those lists, never overrides them.** Why: a move can change where other Tasks are listed (a question aimed at a Member reads its Workflow off the Task it blocks), so a dependent question's placement updates at once; the lists are the one placement every view reads, so the detail must not disagree with them.
- **Round 2, list first (2026-10-09): the word is Workflows wherever a Project's Workflows are meant: the sidebar item, the page's crumb, Settings' nav, ⌘K ("Accounts › Workflows"), G then W, the Edit button (named "Edit the Workflows", its visible text Edit); a Workflow's own name (Bugs) is unchanged, and the line's region stays "Workflow", one Workflow drawn.** Why: a Project has one or more; "Workflow" over a list of five read as one.
- **The pages are `/projects/:key/workflows` (the list), `/projects/:key/workflows/:workflow` (one Workflow's page), `/settings/projects/:key/workflows` (Settings' list, always a list) and `/settings/projects/:key/workflows/:workflow` (one Workflow's editor); the `:workflow` segment is its id, read long or short, or its name ignoring case; the editor reads it against the record as read and goes in place to the id form, so a rename in the draft keeps the address. The old `/workflow` addresses redirect, `?workflow=` becoming the segment, a lone `?step=` naming its Step's Workflow, a lone `?scope=` of a Project of several naming the Workflow its Task is listed in (else the list), every other parameter kept.** Why: the owner picked B, list first, on the mockup board; the address says which Workflow, so a link to one is a link, and old links still land. Round 3 (2026-10-09): Settings' Workflows pages are gone; the editor is `/projects/:key/workflows/:workflow/edit` in the app, and the Settings addresses redirect there.
- **The live list's columns are Workflow · Steps · Waiting · Working · Done today: Waiting is the sum over its Steps of `tasks − working`, Working the sum of `working`, Done today the Tasks done since midnight placed by `listedOn` (`workflow_id`), as the line's "N today". No Median column.** Why: no per-Workflow median is on the wire, and a median of the Steps' medians is not the median of anything: a false figure.

- **One Workflow's page keeps the chip in its crumbs (Project › Workflows › chip): a pick goes to the sibling's address, remembered in the browser as the board's pick; the list never reads the remembered pick. On a phone the "Workflows" crumb steps aside and the Project's mark stands beside the chip with no "/".** Why: the chip is still the phone's way across; the list is the way in, so it must not jump somewhere remembered.
- **Settings' list writes each act at once, one `PUT …/workflow` of the whole graph built from the record as read: `+ Workflow` ("Workflow <count + 1>", stepping up while the name is taken ignoring case, `newWorkflowName`, then its editor with the name focused), ‹ › (`moveWorkflowTo` onto the neighbour; when the move changes where New Tasks start, by `startStep`'s rule, its toast names it: "Moved Triage later. New Tasks start at Investigate."), and the trash through the built delete dialog; the last Workflow's trash is off; one write at a time (a second click in the same moment sends nothing), each said in a toast, a refusal in `/v1`'s words; none is undoable, the editor's ⌘Z covering only its own draft. The editor keeps one draft of the whole graph saved whole on Save.** Why: adding, ordering and deleting Workflows are acts on the list, done when asked; Steps, Connectors and the name are a Workflow's design, drafted and reviewed before Save (decision 1 stands: every write is the whole graph). Round 3 (2026-10-09): the same acts, the same writes, on the app's Workflows list; Settings has no list.
- **The editor of one Workflow has no rail: its head is the Workflow's name as a field (Enter keeps it, Escape puts back the name it had when entered, saved with the draft); a Step moved into another Workflow takes the editor to that Workflow's address with the draft kept; Save opens that Workflow's live page, Cancel Settings' list.** Why: the list is where the Workflows are chosen; this supersedes "a rail of the Workflows above the Step list" above. Round 3 (2026-10-09): Cancel lands on the Workflow's page, as Save does.
- **Round 3, the shell and the navigation (2026-10-09, after the owner's review of round 2; board https://claude.ai/artifact/DNm5PuVXwRj6rJPnCLXFA9, direction B): the shell after Linear — the sidebar flat on the window ground (`--sidebar`), no border; the page a bordered card (`rounded-lg`, 1px `--border`, inset 8px top/right/bottom from `md`, full-bleed on a phone), the kit's `inset` variant with a border in place of its shadow; in dark the ground `--sidebar` (`oklch(0.1 0 0)`) is darker than the card, and the in-card surfaces that painted `bg-sidebar` (the editor's Preview strip, the Blocking graph's bands) paint `bg-muted`, a page surface.** Why: the owner's reference ("the content page will have border background while the navigation is not"); a page surface must not ride the shell's ground token.
- **The bar is two rows in one `<header>`: where you are (the crumbs; the Workflow chip is a crumb), then, only when the page has any, a row named Page (`role="group"`) of what the page does — the view switch and scope at the left, the actions and the one primary at the right; a page with nothing for row 2 has row 1 alone; each row is its own band, a hairline under the crumbs when a second row follows and one under the last row; a phone keeps both rows with icon-only actions, and the fold of round 2 (`BarFold`) is gone, the Workflow page's Line | Blocking | Text included.** Why: "all page related stuff must be on the 2nd line"; with its own row nothing needs folding; a toolbar role would promise a keyboard pattern the row does not have; the owner, on the shipped bar: "Make separate line between first and second header top components" (2026-10-09).

The editor is `/projects/:key/workflows/:workflow/edit` in the app frame (Project › Workflows › name; the Changes chip at the left of row 2, Cancel · Save at the right); Save and Cancel land on the Workflow's page. A Project of one lists its one Workflow, and its Workflow's page names it as a plain crumb (no chip, nothing to pick). An address of a Project of one that carries the line's parameters (`view`, `scope`, `step`, `filter.*`, the by-name filter keys) lands on the Workflow's page, not the list. Settings has no Workflows pages; `/settings/projects/:key/workflows[/:workflow]`, `/settings/projects/:key/workflow` and `/admin/workflow` redirect.** Why: the acts lived only in Settings and read as organisation-level; a plural item landed on one Workflow; the page and its editor must name the same Workflow; round-2 bookmarks of a Project of one carried the line's parameters at the list's address.
- **A Project's settings live under the Project at `/projects/:key/settings/<page>`, General · Members · Labels · Workspaces as tabs on row 2 (a `nav` named "Project settings", `text-xs` segments like the line's), the page's actions and primary at the right of the same row; the sidebar's Settings under a Project opens General and stays marked on every tab. Settings proper (`/settings/*`) is Account + Organisation, reached from the Organisation's menu; its Projects group and New Project are gone. `/settings/projects`, `/settings/projects/:key/<page>`, `/admin/teams[/:key]` and `/admin/workspaces` redirect.** Why: a Project's pages in two navs, one swapping the whole sidebar, was the confusion the owner named; one place per Project, Settings for what sits above Projects.
- **A Project's settings page makes that Project current (it unfolds in the sidebar and is remembered), so `/admin/teams` and `/settings/projects` without a key land on the last Project shown.** Why: the page is under the Project; every page under a Project does this.
